records.title: SUICIDE I Do Not Want To Die

Description:
SUICIDE is preventable. 
By raising awareness and providing resources, we can help save lives.

Suicide is a serious public health problem, and it's great that you're working on a project to raise awareness. Here are some statistics and causes of suicide:

Suicide Statistics:

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), over 700,000 people die by suicide every year.

In the United States, suicide is the fourth leading cause of death among youth ages 15-29 (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention).

Every suicide has a ripple effect, impacting families, friends, and communities.
Causes of Suicide:

Suicide is a complex issue with no single cause. However, some risk factors can increase an individual's vulnerability:

Mental health conditions: Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and substance abuse are all significant risk factors.

Feeling hopeless or trapped: People contemplating suicide may feel like there's no way out of their situation.

Experiencing a loss: The loss of a loved one, job, or relationship can be a trigger.
Bullying and social isolation: These experiences can contribute to feelings of worthlessness and disconnection.

Access to lethal means: Firearms are the most common method of suicide in the United States, highlighting the importance of safe storage.
Family history of suicide: Having a family member who died by suicide can increase one's risk.

Saving Lives:

Here are some things you can include in your project to promote suicide prevention:

Warning Signs: Educate people about the warning signs of suicide, such as talking about wanting to die, social withdrawal, or drastic changes in mood or behavior.

Reaching Out: Encourage people to reach out for help if they are struggling. You can include resources like the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline (988) or crisis text lines.

Reducing Stigma: Stigma surrounding mental health can prevent people from seeking help. Promote open conversations about mental health and suicide prevention.

Building Support Systems: Strong social connections can be a protective factor against suicide. Encourage building healthy relationships and fostering a sense of belonging.

Here are some resources you can reference:

National Suicide Prevention Lifeline: 
988 or https://988lifeline.org/current-events/the-lifeline-and-988/

Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Suicide Prevention): https://www.cdc.gov/suicide/index.html

The Trevor Project (LGBTQ+ Youth Suicide Prevention): 
https://www.thetrevorproject.org/
American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP): 
https://afsp.org/

Remember: Suicide is preventable. 
By raising awareness and providing resources, we can help save lives.

records.title: Rapper Abunai and the Cosmic Brownie Ritual

Description:
It’s one of those strange nights at Cumberland Farms when Rapper Abunai walks in. This time, he’s wearing a see-through plastic cape and a chef’s hat. He looks like he hasn’t slept in days, with wide, wild eyes and a sticky jar in his hand. As he approaches the counter, he reverently places a Cosmic Brownie on a napkin, as if it’s some kind of sacred offering.

Before I can say a word, he reaches into his pocket and pulls out… a can of whipped cream. But he doesn’t put it on the brownie like any normal person would. No, instead, he sprays it all over his hand and smears it across his face like it’s shaving foam, mumbling something about the “blessing of the cosmic brownie.”

Once he’s “prepared” himself, he steps up to the counter, looks at the Cosmic Brownie, and, with complete seriousness, pulls a small bag from his cape filled with… gummy worms coated in something slimy. Without a word, he starts spreading the gummy worms all over the brownie, like he’s creating some high-end, otherworldly dish.

Then, in a move that nobody could have seen coming, he tilts his head back and, yes, begins eating the gummy worms straight off the brownie… hands-free. He hunches over the counter like an animal, whipped cream dribbling from his mouth as he devours the worms one by one, a mixture of spit and cream starting to drip down onto the counter.

At this point, I can’t look away, even though I’m feeling more and more disgusted. But just when I think it can’t get any worse, Rapper Abunai lets out a massive burp—so loud it actually makes a bag of chips on the shelf burst. And, as if it’s the most normal thing in the world, he grabs a rag from the counter, wipes his mouth, and looks at me with a sinister grin: “This is the Cosmic Brownie Ritual.”

In shock, I manage to say, “Dude… that rag is for cleaning the store, not your mouth.” But he just shrugs, picks up what’s left of the brownie, and, without a word, heads out of the store, leaving a sticky trail of whipped cream and gummy worms in his wake.

I never thought I’d have to write “procedure for cleaning up a Cosmic Brownie Ritual” in the store log, but there I am, scrubbing away the mess and wondering if I really saw what I think I just saw.

records.title: Internet Girl, 4TUNAT, Godly the Ruler - KIDS

Description:
Internet Girl on “KIDS”: “Over the years Internet Girl have cultivated their own space bringing and African narrative to an international sound. The song kids reflects on our role as innovators and people trying to follow in our footsteps.”

Godly the Ruler on “KIDS”: “It feels like a lot of the way we talk about youth in music, movies, or any kind of media really has this cloud of romanticization hanging over it…when thats not always the case. There is a lot of suffering in being young, the youth is constantly neglected and counted out. A lot of the times being a young person in the world feels like you’re carrying the weight of the planet on your shoulders or like you’re rolling a boulder up a hill…this song is meant to be a reflection of what it feels like to be young (without the romance filter).”

I started working on this song a year ago, initially with just two chords. Two months ago, I began to develop the arrangement, adding a bridge and refining the structure. I found some old lyrics on my phone that perfectly capture the emotions of someone who has reached their breaking point in a relationship, unsure of what exactly went wrong but knowing it's time to leave. When I tried singing these lyrics over the music, I realized how well they matched the mood and rhythm of the piece.

After many changes during the mixing process, including the addition of multiple instruments, the song has really come together.

I'm excited to share it with you  Stay tuned!

Hello anon. 

Timestamps Season 2 is here. 

Making a track from scratch every day of this month (April) for 30 days and putting it out into the world. Last time I did this was in January of 2022, click the link in my bio if you wanna listen to Season 1 and read up on the lore. 

Day 1 : Cold Shower

I've done a bunch of consecutive day beat series in the past and the intention has always been to kickstart myself into flow state by committing to the daily aspect of it so that there's no room for complacency. It eventually leads me to a point where all the practice from the daily output feeds into projects that I've been trying to finish but haven't been able to.

I watched a video on Basquiat's work ethic and another one on Prince last week. They left me so inspired that I had to get on my shit again and move forward with it.

Today's tune started with the organ riff in the intro and I just jammed out the rest of the parts one after the other. Sort of hit a roadblock with the drums at one point but I had to remind myself to not mull over decisions too much as that's counter-intuitive to the timestamp approach. My ears needed a little break to let go of the bias from hearing it over and over again so I took a cold shower and had a few more tries at it afterwards. Added a few sprinkles here and there, heard it across different speakers and it was done. 

I would have ideally liked to spend less time on it than I did but given that this is Day 1 I'm not so hung up on it. 

The cover art is a photograph I took of my trusted midi keyboard. 

Day 1 succesfully completed.

If you've made it this far, thanks a lot for reading and I'll see you tomorrow.

I find myself caught in the complex emotions of liking someone deeply, yet recognizing that the timing isn't right for us. There's an undeniable connection, and I know you feel it too, but circumstances are not in our favor. So, I've decided to let go and accept that we are better off as friends for now, even though it hurts. I'll move forward, respecting your words and taking a step back before any deeper feelings develop and cause more pain.

I'm not waiting around, but I hold onto hope that maybe in the future, things might change. You're someone who believes in faith, and I trust in fate, so I'm giving our potential some space. Love shouldn't be rushed; it's not a race. Perhaps one day, we'll find a balance between love and friendship, and share peaceful moments together.

For now, I'm choosing to let go, release my hopes of us becoming more, and leave it all to the universe. I'll move on, even though it stings, and I'll trust that if it's meant to be, the universe will guide us back together in its own time.

Description:
Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a mental health condition that is triggered by a terrifying event — either experiencing it or witnessing it. 

Here's a breakdown of the key points:

Trauma-Induced: 
PTSD develops in some people who go through a shocking, scary, or dangerous event. This can include things like war, assault, natural disasters, serious accidents, or even childhood abuse.

Intrusive Memories and Nightmares: People with PTSD experience intense and disturbing thoughts and feelings related to the trauma. This can include flashbacks, nightmares, and overwhelming emotions.

Avoidance: People with PTSD may try to avoid situations or people that remind them of the traumatic event. This can significantly limit their lives.

Changes in Thinking and Mood: Negative changes in thinking and mood are common with PTSD. This can include feeling hopeless, hypervigilance (being on constant high alert), or difficulty concentrating.

Physical Symptoms: PTSD can also cause physical symptoms, such as trouble sleeping, irritability, or difficulty concentrating.

Not everyone who experiences trauma will develop PTSD. Some people may have symptoms for a short time after the event, but they gradually improve. 
However, for others, the symptoms can be long-lasting and disruptive.

Asperger's syndrome, though no longer a formal diagnosis, refers to a set of characteristics that fall within the broader Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). 

People with Asperger's typically experience:

Social difficulties: This can involve trouble understanding social cues, interpreting body language, or engaging in a natural back-and-forth conversation.

Repetitive behaviors and routines: People with Asperger's might find comfort in familiar routines and repetitive actions.

Narrow interests: They may have an intense focus on specific topics and become very knowledgeable about them.

It's important to note that Asperger's was differentiated from other ASD diagnoses by typically not including delays in language development or intellectual disability.

Here's some additional information:

Current Diagnosis: Since 2013, diagnoses have shifted to using ASD as the umbrella term, recognizing the spectrum of presentations.

Self-Identity: Some people who received an Asperger's diagnosis before 2013 still identify with that term. It's a matter of personal preference.

If you'd like to learn more about Asperger's or ASD, here are some resources from reputable organizations:

Autism Speaks: https://www.autismspeaks.org/

National Institute of Mental Health: https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/topics/autism-spectrum-disorders-asd

Asperger's, though not a distinct diagnosis anymore, is a term used to describe a set of symptoms within the Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)  that typically involve challenges in three main areas:

Social Interaction and Communication:

Difficulty making friends and understanding social cues like body language or sarcasm.
Trouble taking turns in conversation or appearing to talk "at" people rather than "with" them.

Unusual speech patterns, like a flat tone or speaking in an overly formal way.

Limited facial expressions or difficulty making eye contact.

Repetitive Behaviors and Routines:

A strong need for routine and discomfort with changes in schedule or environment.

Repetitive movements or actions, like hand flapping or rocking.
Intense focus on specific interests, which can become very detailed and all-consuming.

Sensory Sensitivities:

Overreaction or underreaction to sights, sounds, smells, tastes, or touches. 
For instance, finding loud noises overwhelming or bright lights uncomfortable.

It's important to remember that everyone on the spectrum experiences these traits differently. Some people with Asperger's might have strong social anxieties, while others might struggle more with sensory sensitivities. There's a wide range of variation.

Here are some additional points to consider:

Intellectual Ability: Unlike some other ASD presentations, Asperger's is not typically associated with intellectual disability. People with Asperger's often have average or above-average intelligence.

Language Development: Asperger's also doesn't usually involve delays in language development. People with Asperger's may even have advanced vocabularies in their areas of interest.

If you suspect you or someone you know might have Asperger's or ASD, it's important to consult with a qualified mental health professional for a proper diagnosis and support.

Detroit-bred and Nashville-based singer-songwriter Danny Stevens is ready with his triumphant debut solo LP Better Than You Left Me.
Stevens initially cut his teeth on the indie circuit as the frontman for the seminal pop-rock outfit The Audition - releasing four critically-acclaimed albums, touring the world, and sharing the stage with some of the biggest names in alternative music.
After The Audition, Stevens returned to his roots and began writing the music he had always wanted to create, which references everything from classic Motown soul music and country - to Americana and folk.
While combining these traditional influences together, Stevens also pushes his sound into the modern world by injecting the perfect dose of pop accessibility coupled with tender and vulnerable lyrics that feel both timeless and universally relevant to any listener. "I set out to make an album that sounds like it's for everybody." With an arsenal of songs under his belt, Stevens enlisted the help of prominent Nashville hitmaker and producer Sammy Mitchell (Luke Combs) to lay down the tracks that ultimately became Better Than You Left Me. The result is a hook-laden release that showcases Steven's powerful vocal prowess, a knack for ear-worm melodies, fearless lyricism, and exceptional instrumentation. "I learned to trust myself as a songwriter in this process, and once I did, the floodgates really began to open up" Stevens reflects.

this song, looking back now after a few years, was something that came from the cosmos. Santana moves and operates like that.  He stays in tune with a certain frequency of love, light, expression, creativity, and if you match that frequency you may find yourself in the studio with him.  At least that’s how it seemed to go with this record.  

Heartstrings felt like something divinely orchestrated. I spent a year with no chorus on the record, I had a Big Gigantic saxophone solo where Carlos’s guitar now is, I was frustrated at how slow things were moving with my album, and wanted to get this song done and out.  When it was finished (or i had thought it was finished), I’d taken a bit of time for myself after working on Mariposa (the album this is on).  I remember doing “sober october” for the first time in 2020, meditating in place of substances, trying this spiritual shit out.  One day I was meditating and i got a call from my manager that i felt like taking - he said “carlos santana heard your record and wants to play on it.  he’s free this weekend can we make it up to the Bay”. I obviously couldn’t believe it but was just laughing and thought it was awesome.   As HOV says “ i told my wife this spiritual shit really works”.  who would have thought?  I also learned a big lesson on how with art, sometimes you can’t control the timing and that could be a good thing.  I was happy that it had taken all this time to get the record done, because it was the right time.

days later we’re in the studio caffeinated out of our minds and carlos shows up 10 minutes early and goes on to give a full lesson on Miles Davis before introducing himself and saying he loves the song.  that day in the studio was one of the most informative sessions i’ve had to this day and honestly changed everything about how i see and approach music.

santana, if you know anything about him, sees music as a tool to show people the fullness of themselves - to connect and to heal.  he put me on to where freshness, presence, and power in a sound comes from.  I didn’t understand the strength and seriousness of what we’re doing (of course, all while just playing) but after that day I sort of understood the mission that many musicians have been on before me, that santana took on, and now that I would adapt and bring into the future.

"The trickster is a collective shadow figure, a summation of all the inferior traits of character in individuals. And since the individual shadow is never absent as a component of personality, the collective figure can construct itself out of it continually."
— C.G. Jung

"Trickster" is the fourth single from the debut Supersigil album Spectres.

Comprising 13 experimental tracks produced over the last seven years, Spectres is the 28th release in my discography but my first ever completely solo full-length album. While working on this record, I delved deep into Jungian psychology, concepts from which became central to the project. All 13 tracks are named after archetypes—innate, universal forces that shape our experience of the world.

Spectres is also a visual art project. For each track, I crowd-sourced images submitted in response to the corresponding archetype. These image collections were used to train bespoke Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), simulating the complex interplay between individual psyche and collective unconscious. A further GAN was trained on selected outputs from all the previous GANs, uniting the various archetypes to form an integrated Self.

By limiting the training time of these AI models, I found I could achieve results that mirrored the formation of archetypal symbols as I imagine them deep in our collective unconscious: elusive yet powerful forms emerging from abstract swirls of colour. From thousands of outputs, I selected and manually edited one per archetype to create unique artworks for each track. A collection of 144 further images from this project will be released digitally under the title Spectral Shadows.

Ultimately, Spectres is more than a collection of WAVs and JPGs; it is a dialogue between the personal and the universal, a multidisciplinary exploration of the forces that connect us all. The album has taken me on a transformative seven-year journey through sound, imagery and psyche. In the process, individual and collective experience harmonise, casting a light into the profound depths of human interconnectedness.

Before its official release on 11/23, I'm rolling Spectres out across the web3 ecosystem, dropping tracks on Sound, Zora, Lens and other emerging platforms. In a novel release structure, collectors of individual tracks gain instant access to stream the full album months before its official release. The goal is to push the limits of onchain interoperability to explore what a web3-native album release can look like in 2024.

records.title: DCoop - It's Just Life feat. NE$$Y The Rilla

Description:
NESSY the Rilla and DCoop’s “It's Just Life” - A Celebration of Hip-Hop, Community, and Growth

Inspired by a collective experience fueled by a shared love for music, NESSY the Rilla and DCoop’s track "It’s Just Life" was born out of a weekend pool party aka The VEC Supa Lit Launch where artists and community members came together to exchange energy, passion, and creativity. The track embodies the essence of these moments—capturing the progression of life, personal growth, and unity through the raw lens of hip-hop.

Set against the backdrop of good vibes, sunshine, and open minds, "It’s Just Life" transports listeners to a space where art, culture, and fellowship intersect. NESSY opens with vivid imagery that blends everyday experiences and introspective moments, grounding the track in both reality and reflection. Lines like “French-fries and cold pizza, Shawty on my mind lookin’ like a Mona Lisa” juxtapose the mundane with the divine, while the acknowledgment of life’s ups and downs shine through as he raps, “Had some losses but I’m grateful within.”

As the beat pulses, DCoop’s verse amplifies the song’s communal spirit, painting a picture of an artistic utopia where “the family flew in like a reunion, new homies I swear past lives, ya we knew 'em.” His lyrics flow effortlessly from self-expression to the deeper theme of building together—a notion that’s foundational to hip-hop and echoes throughout the track. The collaborative energy of "Vibe City"—where “beatboxers, MCs, artists, and drummers” unite—underscores the beauty of creation through community.

Together, NESSY and DCoop weave verses that reflect the joy of living in the present, embracing challenges, and flowing through them. The song is not just a celebration of life’s highs but a recognition of its lows, teaching listeners that perseverance and gratitude are at the heart of the journey. The hook, “It’s Just Life, Can’t stress if you do your best,” is an anthem for staying grounded and resilient, a message that reverberates long after the track ends.

What makes "It’s Just Life" more than just a typical hip-hop anthem is its roots in real experiences. That weekend gathering—filled with music, laughter, and collaboration—served as the perfect incubator for these progressive themes to blossom. The synergy between NESSY, DCoop, and their community is felt in every beat, and the result is a track that’s both reflective and uplifting, without veering into clichés.

In "It’s Just Life," NESSY and DCoop don’t just rap about living—they embody it, making the track a testament to the power of music and human connection. Through their verses, the duo delivers a reminder: we all thrive when we grow together, and in the end, it's the shared moments that truly make life worthwhile.

records.title: The Ballad of the Sphinx and the Gryphon

Description:
The Ballad of the Sphinx and the Gryphon -

In the heart of the desert, where sands swirled and temperatures soared, stood two ancient creatures: the sphinx and the gryphon. They faced each other, their eyes locked in a timeless stare. The sphinx's gaze was as steady as the sands, while the gryphon's wings stretched wide, as if ready to take flight.

For millennia, these two creatures had guarded the secrets of the desert, their wisdom etched in the riddles of the ages. They had observed the rise and fall of civilizations, the ebb and flow of time. But now, something was stirring in the depths of the desert, a power that threatened to upset the balance of the ages.

As the stars began to appear in the night sky, the gryphon spoke in tones deep and strong, while the sphinx listened in silence. Their words were whispered in the wind, carried on the scent of sand and spice. The ancient song of their lineage, passed down through the ages, began to coil tight, as if preparing to roar.

In the past, the gods had played their part in the desert's tapestry, their tales woven into the fabric of time. But now, the creatures of the desert had grown weary of their games. The gryphon's trust in the twilight was fading, while the sphinx's eyes, full of sight, began to break free from the bounds of the past.

As the truth emerged from the shifting sands, the sphinx's silent eyes shattered the illusions of the gods. The gryphon's mighty wings lifted off the ground, and together, the two creatures rose against the celestial forces that had ruled them for so long.

Defiant cries rose up to the sky, echoing through the desert, as the sphinx and the gryphon joined forces against their former masters. No longer pawns in a game of fate, they stood as one, their unity a force to be reckoned with.

The desert was no longer a place of ancient secrets and forgotten wisdom. It was a battlefield, where the creatures of the past rose up against the powers that had once ruled them. And in the heart of it all, the sphinx and the gryphon, standing together, their song of defiance ringing out across the sands.

Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), also sometimes called emotionally unstable personality disorder, is a mental health condition that impacts how a person manages their emotions and interacts with others. Here's a breakdown of the key features:

Emotional Instability: People with BPD experience intense and fluctuating emotions that can shift rapidly. These emotions can feel very overwhelming and difficult to control.

Unstable Relationships: BPD is characterized by a pattern of having unstable and intense relationships. There might be an extreme fear of abandonment, leading to clingy behavior or pushing loved ones away. People with BPD may idealize others at first, but then quickly switch to anger or disappointment.

Unhealthy Self-Image:  BPD can cause a shaky sense of self-identity. Self-perception can be unclear or frequently changing. This can be linked to constantly seeking approval from others.

Impulsive Behaviors: BPD can lead to impulsive and risky behaviors that can be self-damaging. This might involve reckless spending, substance abuse, unsafe sex, or self-harm.

Suicidal Ideation:  People with BPD are at a higher risk for suicidal thoughts or attempts, especially during emotional crises.

It's important to remember that BPD can manifest differently in each person. Not everyone will experience all of these symptoms, and the severity can vary.

Here are some resources where you can learn more about BPD:

It’s about dreaming of a castle not built on the illusion of opportunity but rooted in an environment where love and freedom to exist are given, not privileges. This song captures a longing for a space where authenticity thrives, unshackled by societal expectations.

In a world where fake AI artists are celebrated, I wanted to push back with something raw and real—imperfect, unplanned, and completely vulnerable. This track is a collection of memories that have shaped how I love, live, and show up in the world. It’s unapologetically unpolished, an experiment in honesty.

For a long time, my health - both mental and physical - was on a decline, with no clear path back to a state of normalcy.

I started playing drums when i was 6 years old and always wanted to make music when i would be older. Seven years ago when i was 16, I started a formal education in music and sound design, which unexpectedly led me into the trap music scene. There, I achieved significant success, including producing a chart-topping song and contributing to various projects, some of which were featured in a Netflix series or other significant projects. Despite these accomplishments, my true passion has always been for ambient music, a preference I had sidelined for the allure of trap music's popularity.

As my health issues became more worse, the joy I once found in creating music began to fade, turning what was once a passion into a burden. By 2023, I had nearly ceased making music altogether due to my declining health. However, I've always maintained a positive mindset, although holding onto it became increasingly challenging as my health worsened.

In December 2021, a trip to Los Angeles to work on music and collaborate with my manager in local studios marked a significant turning point. It was during this time that I felt truly alive for the first time in a long while. This experience underscored the importance of maintaining a positive outlook and recognizing opportunities even in difficult times, reaffirming my inherent optimism.

After I came back home, everything started to get worse again.


Until now.

I feel a positive change in my health (it's slow, but it's something).

The discovery of 432Hz music was a revelation, resonating deeply with me and aiding in my sleep and overall well-being. This newfound connection led me to fully embrace ambient music under my own name, aligning more closely with my authentic self. This transition not only signifies a return to my true musical interests but also serves as an invitation for listeners to join me on a journey of healing and self-discovery.

Deciding to share my story and songs on places like "Sound" is kicking off a new chapter for me and might light up the way for others who are going through tough times. Going back to my old tracks and adding new vibes and what I've learned along the way is a cool way to show how much I've grown, both in my life and in my music.

As I keep going down this road, I gotta remember that my story and beats could really hit home for a lot of folks. Being real and open about what I've been through can help create a vibe where everyone feels like they're part of something bigger, pushing them to find their own way to heal and discover themselves.

I'm hoping that diving into ambient music not only does wonders for me but also reminds others about how powerful music can be in fixing what's broken inside. It's all about staying true to who you are. My journey's a clear sign that even when things look bleak, there's always a way to find a bit of light and get back that spark through the stuff we love doing.

- JZ

A non-fungible token (NFT) is a unique digital identifier for audio that is recorded on a blockchain and used to certify ownership and authenticity. It cannot be copied, substituted, or subdivided.[1] Ownership of an NFT is recorded on the blockchain and can be transferred by the owner, allowing NFTs to be sold and traded. NFTs can be created by anyone, and require little to no coding skills to create. NFTs typically contain references to digital files such as artwork, photos, videos, and audio. Because NFTs are uniquely identifiable, they differ from cryptocurrencies, which are fungible.

I wrote this song when I visited Atlanta for the first time. Fueled by the musical energy from the city, I channeled my stresses away and dreams into reality. For my senior year physics capstone, two friends and I decided to build a fully self-sustainable tiny house. This required us to work long hours every weekend, but one weekend I was booked for a studio session and music conference in Atlanta. I was stressed out for missing a grueling weekend of work, but music quickly brought me back. I was in Atlanta pursuing my dream, so I told myself, “don’t stress.” The song quickly took shape after that. 

As the hook says, “life is gonna push your buttons but don't stay pressed.” This is me reminding myself that life will always be hard, things will always go in directions you don’t expect, and to stay flexible throughout the process. This song reminds me that you don’t always have control, so “don’t stress, no please don’t stress.” The verses explore my struggle with these stresses and how, at the end of the day, I’m trusting the process like farmers with fruit. I tend to my goals, hoping one day they bloom. This also relates to my experience volunteering at a community garden throughout my college years, which showed me how this process occurs. I hope you enjoy it, and thank you for your support!!

This song is a metacommentary on my life over the last 4~ or so years. 

Performance Anxiety is an instrumental I have been working on since 2019, with guitar and bass recordings from 2021, and combined with lyrics I wrote and performed in 2024. In the future I hope to be less ensnared within my actual performance anxiety, and I’m trying to be okay with posting music with less formal preparation beforehand. Build in public, as they say.

In 2018-19, I was about to release my debut album and take on the world with a tour in the Denver area. Then, as the release got closer and closer, and the pandemic worsened, two dams broke at once. At the same time as the pandemic made it practically impossible to make a career as a real life events performer, so too did my mental health fall apart as I lost my job.

I was so socially anxious that I could not even use social media at one point - the act itself felt like a performance, for an infinite mocking audience whose standards I could not meet. Really, I was placing unhealthy and unrealistic standards upon myself, as an independent artist, - trying to compete with bigger brand names, and book DJing gigs at festivals and travel for shows. I was just trading mental health for a chance at what I really wanted - an independent career.

I hope this artwork makes you feel something real.

ABOUT ALTER MY DIRECTION

Alter My Direction is the third song on a 3-song EP called Branches. It concludes the story arc of moving on from the ending of a relationship. With every relationship that ends, while I retain scars, I also come away with new strengths and new insights on where I need to improve. Lessons learned about myself and others are what help me grow. Once the dust settles, I can move forward in life — toward personal goals and new relationships — and sometimes it requires altering my direction in life.


“The cuts run deep under my skin,
and my callused fingertips
keeping me afloat out here."

I may have new scars and calluses from a previous relationship, but upon a closer look at them, they are key to who I am today, and can help me grow into who I want to be.


“Like a wild horse on the run,
I’ve got a destination, but I’m lost.
Now the plain ahead is all there is to see."

Sometimes it’s hard to know where you’re headed even though you know where you want to go. And sometimes, for me, even if I feel lost, it’s the movement, the taking action, that changes things for the better. This lyric influenced the song artwork.


“See what I mean to me, an honest look at my reflection.
Not as over as it seems, chase it now, alter my direction."

Taking an honest look in the mirror at myself — the good, the bad, and the ugly — and learning from it is how I can move forward in life. I try to do this regularly, but sometimes the ending of a relationship forces me to do this at a higher level.


OTHER INTERESTING NOTES

Alter My Direction (as well as whole EP) was co-produced by me (Mike Bass), Alara, and Steven LaFashia. This was my first time working with other producers, and enjoyed the process very much!

The Branches EP was recorded at Retro City Studios in Philadelphia, PA.

Alter My Direction blends more into the indie pop genre, which is new for me. The same goes for the EP as a whole, which has dream pop, indie folk, and indie pop elements.

"Short Temper" is my raw, honest take on toxic relationships. I wrote this track after dealing with a narcissistic and alcoholic ex, and let me tell you, it was a rollercoaster. If you've ever felt like you're walking on eggshells around someone you love, this song is for you. I poured all that frustration, pain, and eventual self-realization into these lyrics and beats.

The deep house vibes mixed with chill elements mirror the ups and downs of a relationship that's beautiful one moment and chaotic the next. When I sing "Short, short, short Temper," it's that moment of clarity when you finally see the pattern you've been stuck in.

This track is more than just a song to me - it's a reminder that it's okay to walk away from something that's hurting you, even if it's hard. If you've been there, I hope "Short Temper" helps you feel seen and gives you the strength to prioritize your peace. Remember, you deserve better than someone's short temper.

Despite my impossible task I travel onwards, for the alternative is far too grim to comprehend. In my youth my fears were tangible. A scraped knee. A broken bone. The untimely demise of those I share infinite love for. This dread that hangs above my head, thirsting for my end, is farther than any wicked conjuration my mind has plagued me with all throughout my life. It would be absurd, in a way, if I could not feel the pumping of my blood, the heat behind my ears, the screaming of every cell in my body pressing me onwards towards the unpromised relief of shelter. I came here with a mission objective and have found only hell. Ruins. A Sisyphean cycle in which I find my fingertips not pressed against the boulder, but clenched tightly into my sweat soaked palms, fleeing ever downhill from an enormous force of malice that seems to torture me by design. Embark on a journey through the genesis and evolution of "Broken Melodies," a song that delves into the depths of heartbreak and betrayal. Explore the intricacies of its creation, from the raw emotion of its inception to the cathartic release of its final production.

Inception

"Broken Melodies" emerges from the depths of despair, a testament to the songwriter's journey through the wreckage of a shattered romance. Inspired by personal experiences of betrayal and loss, the song serves as a vessel for emotional expression and introspection. With each lyric and melody, the songwriter confronts their pain head-on, transforming heartache into artistry and forging a path toward healing.

Lyricism

The lyrics of "Broken Melodies" paint a vivid portrait of love gone awry, capturing the raw emotion and turmoil of a fractured relationship. From the haunting verses to the anthemic chorus, every word resonates with raw honesty and vulnerability. The imagery of broken melodies and twisted symphonies serves as a poignant metaphor for the dissonance and discord that permeate the protagonist's world. Through poetic introspection, the songwriter lays bare their innermost thoughts and emotions, inviting listeners to share in their journey of self-discovery and redemption.

Melodic Alchemy

The melody of "Broken Melodies" is a haunting fusion of emotion and artistry, crafted with precision to mirror the ebb and flow of the protagonist's tumultuous journey. The melancholic chord progressions and soaring vocals evoke a sense of longing and melancholy, while the pulsating rhythm underscores the urgency and intensity of the emotional narrative. With each crescendo and refrain, the music builds to a cathartic release, offering solace and redemption in the face of heartache and despair.

Production

In the studio, "Broken Melodies" undergoes a transformation, evolving from a mere concept into a fully-realized sonic landscape. The songwriter meticulously crafts each layer of instrumentation, infusing the music with depth and texture. From the haunting piano melodies to the ethereal synthesizers, every element is carefully orchestrated to enhance the song's thematic resonance and evoke an immersive listening experience.

Conclusion

"Broken Melodies" stands as a testament to the resilience of the human spirit and the cathartic power of artistic expression. Through its evocative lyricism, haunting melody, and meticulous production, it invites listeners to embark on a journey of self-discovery and healing. As the final notes fade into the ether, the echoes of this poignant anthem linger, a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there is beauty to be found in brokenness.

With "Broken Melodies," the songwriter has not only crafted a captivating piece of music but also forged a connection with listeners, inviting them to find solace and redemption in shared experiences of love and loss. May this exploration enrich your appreciation of the song and inspire you to embrace the beauty of brokenness.

It was my last night in Poland before returning to the US when I wrote this hook. Driven by the light-heartedness of the beat, I came to realize that this is my life right now and change is out of my control. I wanted it to be simple and relatable since life can become so complicated. Oftentimes, making music helps me simplify my issues, so I tried to bring that energy into this song. For me, this vibe clears my mind and helps me lock into what is actually important around me. It's that deep breath you take when you feel too much weight on your back and are finally able to release it. Smile because you can, not because you need to. I want to inject the feelings of dopamine and serotonin within this track.

In the verses, I tried to break down the issues I battle with such as greater purpose in life, external pressures, and underachieving. By the end of the second verse, I say, “hit or miss you still land somewhere, so go there, go learn there, it’s probably for the best, lost a piece well it's chess, got my mates and my check, so I’m winning, I guess?” This reminds me to keep pushing throughout your journey despite any expectations, and to stay curious. Oftentimes, it can turn out better than you expected. Thank you for listening, and I hope you enjoy the vibe!

Downtempo future bass is a genre that combines slow, mesmerizing rhythms with rich bass lines and futuristic synthesizers. Songs in this style often create an atmosphere of deep immersion and relaxation, inviting the listener to enjoy a musical journey through soundscapes.

In a typical downtempo future bass composition, one can expect soft, smooth transitions between chords, framed by spatial effects and often complemented by vocal samples or plaintive vocals. This creates a sense of emotional depth and introspection, making the music ideal for moments of reflection or relaxation.

The instrumental filling in such tracks usually includes not only traditional electronic elements but also organic sounds, such as piano or strings, which gives the music warmth and liveliness. The rhythms, though slowed down, maintain clarity and order, emphasizing each bass beat and creating a unique sound space characteristic of the genre

This song is dedicated to all the amazing people who have worked tirelessly to develop the PXNKAP3 project, as well as the tremendous PXNKAP3 community. I wrote this song to be released in celebration of the official PXNKAP3 minting on February 7, 2024. 

The idea to write a song for the PXNKAP3 project and community came to me just a few days prior to the mint date as I began playing around with lyrical ideas related to the project's offerings. I decided to put my writing and production skills to the test to see if I could fully complete the song in just under 3 days, and after a couple of sleepless nights, I successfully reached my goal. 

This song was a ton of fun to write; I wanted to allude to as many of the rich offerings of the PXNKAP3 project as possible while still keeping the song short and to-the-point. It took a few attempts to land on a vocal style for this song, and while I don't typically sing punk rock, I think I found something that worked well enough. On guitar, it was a blast slamming out power chords and trying to keep on tempo for all of the rapid muted downstrokes. The solo was one of the more challenging parts of the song to write since I was under such a time crunch, and I ended up altering part of the song form in order to make the solo fit better. This was also the first time I recorded with my bass guitar as I just recently brought it into my arsenal. And as tedious as it is to hand sequence drums, I really love the process as well as the result. 

I used Reaper as my DAW, and I recorded, edited, and mixed all of the guitars, bass, and vocals in my home studio. Credit goes to my partner for her vocal contribution on the choruses. I used a Studio Projects C1 microphone, a Schecter Diamond Series Garza Signature Edition electric guitar, and a Cort Curbow 52 bass guitar. I hand sequenced the drum parts into a MIDI editor, played through the GetGood Drums Matt Halpern Signature Kit in Kontakt 7. I used a host of plugins for mixing and mastering primarily from Native Instruments, iZotope, Kazrog, and Waves. 

After years of work as a composer, sound designer, and technical audio designer in the games industry, I’m happy to be working on my own personal music again. The minting of this song marks the second song I’ve minted, as well as the second song I’ve produced in 2024, the first being an acapella song titled Art Needs You that I wrote for the Optimism “We Love the Art” on chain art contest. Original minting link here: https://highlight.xyz/mint/659c207641fad46b6bc0e21b

I hope y’all enjoy the song! Thanks for checking it out and for reading a bit about it and my process!

~Joshua

I crafted 'Vibrate Higher' with a deep understanding of music as the essence of vibration itself. Every sound in this piece is a testament to this belief, created from the everyday objects that surrounded me at the time. The comb, the tape machine, my TR-08, a harmonica, and my voice—all came together in a symphony of vibrations that now form 'Vibrate Higher.'

In this song, I wanted to explore the idea that music can elevate our consciousness, and what better way to do so than by using the very vibrations that permeate our existence? The title itself, 'Vibrate Higher,' encapsulates this journey—an invitation to transcend through sound.

By repurposing household objects as instruments, I aimed to blur the lines between the ordinary and the extraordinary. The hum of the tape machine, the haunting cry of the harmonica, and the rhythmic pulse of the TR-08—all of these elements were carefully chosen to create a sonic landscape that resonates with authenticity.

Through the composition process, I felt like an alchemist, transforming raw sounds into a cohesive whole. Each note, each beat, became a building block in a symphony that speaks to the soul.

My voice, amidst this symphony of vibrations, serves as a familiar guide—a reminder that this is not just music, but a deeply personal expression of self. As the song unfolds, listeners are invited to join me on a journey of sonic exploration, to vibrate higher and discover the limitless possibilities of sound.

'Vibrate Higher' is more than just a song to me; it's a testament to the transformative power of music. It's a reminder that inspiration is all around us, waiting to be discovered in the most unexpected places. Through this piece, I hope to connect with listeners on a deeper level, inviting them to tune in, elevate their consciousness, and experience the magic of vibrations.

Time is a flat circle in digital physics. We can travel backwards, forwards or just endlessly circle the present in a sea of memes. To be online is to be free of the constraints of the physical world. We can travel through layers of digital space, summoning and transforming culture, and in the process perform acts of communal mythmaking as pioneers codifying what it means to live in a fully networked world.

Starholder explores our transition into this networked society. It embraces the freedom offered by digital physics to transcend time, space and the shackles of traditional media forms. SOY is the manifestation of a person's break from the mandates and prejudices of their life. It's a process that everyone experiences at some point, each in their own way and with their own "monsters." Because it is both a universal and personal experience, we asked our audience to help us write the lyrics. Through Instagram stories, they contributed their phrases to write the RAP for the song.

It was composed, recorded, and produced in our home during the quarantine, a time of introspection that allowed us to mature this work and learn that we are capable of expressing all the sounds we imagine.

It was mastered by our friend and colleague Maxi Frini from Spain. Additionally, it featured the collaboration of independent actors who brought the "monsters" of the introduction to life with their voices.

DJ Mariano Torres also collaborated by using his vinyl records to represent the "monsters" throughout the song.

This work allowed us to create synergy.

SOY is not just ours, it belongs to EVERYONE.

<The Story Behind This Work>

Two years ago, during a summer when Karen was 11 years old, she was struggling with depression and felt desperate.

It was the encouragement from a now-deceased benefactor, who was fighting his own battle with illness while shining with the will to create the era of web3, that allowed her to take the first step into this world.

He had been living for several years since his terminal diagnosis and shared with her that "There must be a reason you're still alive, and when you find your role in the next world, it will be time to depart," along with the baton he passed to her.

"Shadows of My Soul" started as a reflection of my own struggles, born from the ups and downs of everyday life. As I wrote each line, I poured my emotions onto the page, blending my challenges and victories into the chorus. With every note and melody, I aimed to create a connection, reaching listeners in a way that felt familiar and deeply relatable.

"Stone" hits close to home for me. It's about what it feels like to love someone who just doesn't let you in, you know? Like you're constantly hitting a wall. It's really about that push and pull – wanting to be close, yet needing your own space because sometimes, that closeness can be too much when it's not fully returned. Writing this song was like a heart-to-heart with myself, realizing it's okay to want more and it's okay to say, 'Hey, I need a minute.' It's pretty much me learning out loud that taking care of myself isn't selfish. It's necessary.

Crank up the volume and brace for a blast of neon-lit nostalgia with "NGMI (Dreams In The Red)," the latest single from the enigmatic virtual sensation, The Crew. Fresh from the digital mind of Sam Ellis, aka "thepencil.eth," this track is a gleeful dive into the not-so-serene side of the crypto world, wrapped in the trappings of bombastic 80s glam rock.

"NGMI (Dreams In The Red)" pulls no punches, tapping into the tongue-in-cheek, often self-deprecating humor that thrives within the cryptocurrency community. NGMI, or "Not Gonna Make It," serves as a playful yet poignant nod to the despair of watching digital fortunes dip into the crimson. Through thunderous riffs and a palpable sense of urgency, the song encapsulates the emotional rollercoaster that is investing in the volatile crypto market.

Here are the heart-thumping, chart-crashing lyrics that capture the collective groan of every trader watching their dreams dip and dive:

Not gonna make it,
I'm not gonna make it right now
Not gonna make it
The charts are so red
and they have me feeling so down

The charts look bleak, 
so cold and so stark
Full throttle down, 
but who sank this arc?!
I'm too broken to wager
Couldn't chase the green; 
it's a stranger
But how could I have known, 
it would crash, undone
Just by dreaming of numbers in the sun

I'm not gonna make it,
I'm not gonna make it right now
Not gonna make it
The charts are so red
and they have me feeling so down

The song isn't just a lament; it's a rallying cry—a reminder that in the fast-paced world of crypto, today's reds are tomorrow's greens. It captures a moment of levity in the face of financial uncertainty, encouraging a camaraderie among those who might feel the pinch of a market downturn.

"NGMI (Dreams In The Red)" is not only a continuation of The Crew's unique blend of crypto culture with retro rock vibes, but it's also a bold statement about enduring through the highs and lows, all while keeping a sense of humor. As part of their debut album, this track ensures that The Crew is not just here to play music; they're here to soundtrack the experience of a new generation of digital dreamers and daring investors. So, whether you're up or down today, let The Crew rock you back to a place where every day holds the promise of a bullish turnaround.

Velvet Meadow throws us a curve ball with his new single "When The Moment Comes". He wanted to capture something fresh in the realm of indie pop. Bringing his Fiance/artwork artist Cameron Cox along with the recording process. Velvet wrote the instrumentation with his old 1980s Poly 61 synthesizer while house sitting for a friend in St Augustine Beach FL. After numerous attempts to add his own vocals to it without success, he played with the idea of seeing if Cameron would want a go at it. After a couple takes they had the song ready for the mixing phase. 

"It was a pretty cool experience. We had to house sit my friends beach house for 2 weeks. It was like a free vacation. I brought all of my gear with me, and on one nice day I set up everything outside with the greatest views possible. Wrote the song all day along with maybe p**sing off some neighbors, I don't know haha. I couldn't get a good vocal melody for the life of me, and almost threw the track out until I had the idea of seeing if Cameron would give it a go. I remember absolutely loving the producing side of this track. I went HAM with effects, and tricks Ive gathered along the way. I hope everyone likes it as much as I do!" - Kris Heironimus

A few years ago, in the heart of Miami, I created my second song, 'Count Me.' It was a melody born not just from chords and lyrics but from a profound place within me—a place of reflection, resilience, and a burning desire to be seen.
I found myself at a reoccurring theme within my life. It was a realization that the people around me, friends I thought would stand by, seemed to be 'counting me out.' In their eyes, perhaps, my dreams didn't echo the greatness and depth I saw. It was a significant moment, a turning point that inspired 'Count Me.'
The lyrics flowed with each word a testament to the battles fought, the doubts faced, and the relentless spirit within. Life had thrown curveballs, and I'd been down and out more times than I could count. People predicted failure, expected me to crumble and fade away, but every single time, I rose from the ashes, triumphant.
With each note, 'Count Me' became more than a song—it evolved into my personal anthem. A lyrical mirror reflecting back the strength I discovered within myself. It's a reminder that the only belief I truly need is my own. The journey from doubt to triumph speaks not only to the struggles of the past but also to a constant commitment to self-pride. It's a musical letter to my younger self, an encouragement to the person I am today. 'Count Me' isn't just a song; it's a celebration of unwavering self-belief.
Releasing it as my Sound XYZ debut is a significant moment unveiling a piece of my soul, a vulnerable yet empowering message to the world. This song is my gift to those who've faced doubts and setbacks, a melody that whispers, KEEP GOING!
Sharing this fun and heartwarming affirmation with the world is my way of saying, COUNT YOURSELF IN! The journey might be tough, but every step is a victory. To everyone listening, I'm proud of you. Keep believing, keep striving, and always count yourself in <3

“The Blue Rush” is more than just a song—it’s a self-portrait in sound. Named after the handle I've used online for years, this track embodies my musical identity, balancing the delicate and the bold. It starts with simple, catchy melodies and confessional, clean guitar tones, reflecting my introspective side. But as it unfolds, it surges into what has always been at the core of my passion: loud, expressive electric guitar.

This song is a return to the essence of what drives me as a musician. It’s an exploration of contrast—gentle yet intense, melodic yet raw—capturing both the precision of my playing and the unfiltered emotion behind it. “The Blue Rush” is not just a composition; it’s a statement, a sonic representation of who I am and where my music is heading.

'cloud 9' is a part of my 単​に​RetroFuture album. The ethereal vibe is something I like to tap into with my releases. This track definitely shows off my inspirations from 90's old school hip hop, trip-hop artists like Bonobo, and contemporary lo-fi hip hop artists such as Vanilla and Wun Two.

It was the classic tale of a producer and artist in a studio when Nate Reed put together a loop that spurred a catchy yet truthful hook in my head: “I feel like I'm falling down, but the sun is rising and the clouds are passing.” This hook represents my mind being consumed by the pressures of finishing college with a physics degree and trying to build a foundation for my musical career. I was grinding hard every day, and the end was in sight. Soon, the clouds would pass, and my path for the future would become clear.

The verses touch on the topics of my future and the pressures that are to come. I know this path is one full of doubt and obstacles, so I need to believe in myself and do it for the love I have for the craft. The work I do must be enough, as the clout and fame that come with the job are full of disillusionment. As I mature as an artist, these lessons become more and more vivid. Thank you for checking out the track, and I hope this energy resonates with you!

The song resonates with anyone striving to find their place in the world, reminding us that the journey is as important as the destination, and that true fulfillment comes from following one's heart and soul.

Detroit-bred and Nashville-based singer-songwriter Danny Stevens is ready with his triumphant debut solo LP Better Than You Left Me.
Stevens initially cut his teeth on the indie circuit as the frontman for the seminal pop-rock outfit The Audition - releasing four critically-acclaimed albums, touring the world, and sharing the stage with some of the biggest names in alternative music.
After The Audition, Stevens returned to his roots and began writing the music he had always wanted to create, which references everything from classic Motown soul music and country - to Americana and folk.
While combining these traditional influences together, Stevens also pushes his sound into the modern world by injecting the perfect dose of pop accessibility coupled with tender and vulnerable lyrics that feel both timeless and universally relevant to any listener. "I set out to make an album that sounds like it's for everybody." With an arsenal of songs under his belt, Stevens enlisted the help of prominent Nashville hitmaker and producer Sammy Mitchell (Luke Combs) to lay down the tracks that ultimately became Better Than You Left Me. The result is a hook-laden release that showcases Steven's powerful vocal prowess, a knack for ear-worm melodies, fearless lyricism, and exceptional instrumentation. "I learned to trust myself as a songwriter in this process, and once I did, the floodgates really began to open up" Stevens reflects.

In "意义之网" (translated as "Web of Meaning"), the 5th single from our upcoming album 'Endless Summer' (无尽夏日), Davyd and I delve into the intricate webs we spin in our lives and the struggle to break free from them. This track explores the paradox of human existence—how we craft our own meanings, only to find ourselves ensnared by them.

The lyrics touch on the mysterious and often whimsical nature of human behaviour—our secrets, impulsive decisions, and fleeting thoughts. There's an irony in how we chase every moment, fearing wasted time, yet often end up exhausted, flying aimlessly without clear direction. As I sing, "每个人头上的光环，熠熠生辉" ("The halo above each person’s head shines brightly"), it highlights how our pursuits give us a purpose, even though we are the ones who assign meaning to these purposes in the first place.

Davyd described working on this track as "a beautiful musical escape," a sentiment that resonates in the chorus, which repeatedly reminds us of the "意义之网" ("Web of Meaning") we've woven. The refrain "无法逃脱" ("unable to escape") underscores the reality of this entanglement, guiding the listener through a reflective journey on the complexities of our choices and the meanings we create. It invites us to ponder what truly makes life meaningful or meaningless, especially when these concepts are born from the meanings our culture and civilisation impose.

"意义之网" aims to provoke thought on the delicate balance between the creation of meaning and the entrapment it can bring.

“Route 666” is an electronic track that exudes aggression and intensity from the very first beat. The track’s foundation is a fierce, driving rhythm that hits hard and fast, embodying the spirit of the notorious highway it’s named after. Layered atop this relentless beat are various atmospheric sounds that create a sense of unease and foreboding, painting an aural picture of a journey through a dystopian landscape.

The track’s aggressive nature is further amplified by the use of distorted synths and dark, brooding basslines that weave in and out of the soundscape. “Route 666” is not just a song; it’s an experience that transports the listener to a world where the thrill of danger and the allure of the unknown reign supreme. It’s a piece that’s sure to resonate with fans of hard-hitting electronic music who appreciate a track that can both energize and unsettle.
This song is about love, questions about one’s own approach towards it and wondering how permanent things can actually be.

As the artist behind 'Luna Lights,' I wanted to create an experience that feels like stepping into another realm. This track merges dark pop with ethereal electronic elements, blending atmospheric layers of deep bass, haunting synths, and ambient textures to craft a soundscape that pulls you into a dreamlike journey. It’s a space for introspection, where the subtle interplay of minimalist beats and haunting melodies reflects a sense of mystery and emotion, giving it that cinematic, otherworldly feel.

I aimed to build a production that feels both immersive and hypnotic, where reflective lyrics meld seamlessly with the sound palette. It’s for listeners who love to dive deep into atmospheric and emotive tracks, especially those who appreciate the experimental side of pop. As the deep bass pulses beneath the ethereal melodies, 'Luna Lights' invites you on a surreal and haunting ride, capturing the essence of dark pop.

Expect deep basslines intertwined with ambient layers, atmospheric textures, and moody synths, all woven together to create an ethereal and introspective tone. If you're drawn to dreamy, haunting pop with emotional depth, this track is for you.

I wrote this song over winter break during my junior year of college. During this break, I was struggling to complete projects due to overthinking, so I found a random beat online and sat there until I wrote the full song. The idea was for it all to be recorded in one take. This would give me practice with writing and recording longer takes. Throughout the process, I started to enjoy the song more and more. I was able to let go of any expectations of song structure and just write. The song title stems from this idea, "ya ya ya," to show it is what it is.

A short yet catchy hook followed by bars that encapsulate my mind in the moment. Residual feelings of my breakup mixed with feelings of new experiences gave me a way to discuss my current mental state. A bit confused but pushing forward, and at the same time showing self-love and love for others. The constant switching of flows represents how I was playing around. This song represents a stream of consciousness that contemplates my past, present, and future. I hope this resonates with you, and thank you!

Dominican-American artist Esty is a lot of things—a singer, rapper, and songwriter, a skilled roller skater, a lover of all things very cute, and a strong presence on both Instagram and TikTok. Over the past few years especially, she’s cultivated a signature sound: a surprising mix of future-warped dembow and sonic nods to anime dipped in electronic alt-pop. Singing and rapping in Spanglish, the Venice, California-based artist promotes an empowering union of emotional vulnerability and personal strength. The melodies are earwormy but fresh; Esty’s music is quickly identifiable as her thing. She is a singular force. 
Earlier collabs include tracks with Andra Day, Chris Brown, Tyga, Fuego, STINT, Xiuhtezcatl, Sango, Ale Alberti (Anitta, Alesso), Avedon (Chloe x Halle, Megan Thee Stallion), Bassto (Jorja Smith, Koffee), Anwar Sawyer (Audrey Nuna) and Luyo (J Balvin, Anitta). Also over the course of her career, she’s teamed up with major brands like Puma, Nike, Urban Outfitters, Burberry, Metro by T-Mobile, Target, Lexus, and Urban Decay. 

Later this year, Esty will drop a new LP, too. Already a luminary for hundreds of thousands, 2024 is the year she’ll soar out of breakout playlists, like Spotify’s Mixto, Fresh Finds and Apple Music’s New Music Daily, and into exponential growth. She’s begun to showcase her discography live: at the Grand Park LA NYE Countdown opening for Duckwrth and Kinky and broadcasted by Fuse TV, and at an LA Clippers vs NY Knicks Halftime Show. Having solidified her unmistakable style, this is the year in which Esty will hit new, massive highs.

After the end of a six year relationship I didn't want to sit down with my feelings and really process what happened. I distracted myself with videogames, friends and just hanging out around the house. That changed the moment one of those friends recommended a show to me on Netflix and I had to sit down and feel what was going on inside myself. Not even 5 minutes into the show I grabbed my acoustic guitar and started singing the first lines that eventually would become 'Piece Of Me'. That night I wrote the song, recorder it and produced it entirely.  From heartbreak straight into the music, that's Piece Of Me, nothing more and nothing less.

WHY I DO WHAT I DO 

I have to do what I do… I’m an artist at the soul level and writing, singing, producing and performing music is the best way for me to make sense of the world and myself. In turn, if I can make the listener feel understood, happier, connected to a greater whole then my job is done - that’s my definition of success in the music industry - touching hearts.

I’ve been in this full time since 2019 and it’s the only thing I do. As a writer/producer/singer I’ve gathered over 100 million streams and as a solo artist over 30 million streams.

MY SOUND GENESIS

I believe that the Sound.xyz community has the potential to get what I’m trying to build in this new day and age and would like to be in this with me for the long haul.

Being on the edge of tech with a meaningful approach and solid plan is something that I’m sure the Sound.xyz collectors will appreciate. 

So this is my genesis track on Sound, and the first drop of a three-part series over the next couple months. Collectors that mint this drop get a free Limited Edition of my next drop on Sound, and I’m using the proceeds from this drop to buy each collector a $4.99 edition of my Digital EP off of Vault.fan as an extra gift for them. 

I’m not here to make a quick buck, I’m here to build a community of tech enthusiasts, music enthusiasts and frontrunners in a new wave. 

After releasing music for six years straight, doing therapy for my cPTSD I've decided this year to not burn myself out and really focus inward on what I need. 'Too Heavy' is me being candid about what is going on beneath the surface a lot of the days. It's a peek behind the curtain in my psyche as I try to build something new and exciting in 2024 and beyond. It's why I'm changing strategies this year and not putting as much pressure on myself like I used to do because life, for me, often is 'Too Heavy'.

This approach to music and music ownership combined with the direct to listener and likeminded hearts is something that fires me up to no end!

WHY YOU SHOULD CARE

I’ve been doing this since 2010 when I was 20 after visiting NYC and dreaming about what I should do with my life. I came back to Europe and started using the internet to teach myself how to write music, sing songs, produce tracks, perform and play guitar in my Mom’s basement for three years in solitude. 

I played the drums for seven years, from 7 years old until about 14. But I was always captivated by guitar, guitar solos and piano from a young age. So besides guitar (my main instrument) I produce all my own music (at least 90% of it) and I pretty much use any instrument I can find as long as it adds to my music and universe I'm trying to create.

Fun Fact: I was into Bitcoin mining well over a decade ago and bought a pizza with it back then… I don’t even remember the pizza.

I started playing live on stages in 2013 and then in 2018 I released my first single on Spotify: “I’m Gone”. It never got more than 100 streams but I released the second single a month later because I know what I’m building: a community, a tribe, a group of like minded and warm compassionate people.

Fun Fact: I owned and operated one of the biggest Rockstar Games fan sites in the world from 2008 until 2013. Got flown out to NYC 2 times by Rockstar, once to play ‘Max Payne 3’ and a second time to play GTA ONLINE before it hit the public.

What I believe is that there are many many people out there with very similar life experiences but don’t have ways to process it. I love to be that conduit for my listeners while at the same time exploring new avenues of consuming, distributing and experiencing the music and my life story.

WHAT’S NEXT

I’ve been releasing music since 2018 and I’m so thankful for everything I’ve achieved. Yet I think that a lot of my current songs didn’t get the love and appreciation that I think they deserved. This year is focussed on me building a solid live act, getting people into the fold of what I’m building before I’m releasing brand new and amazing music in 2025 and supporting my current body of work.

However, letting those brand new songs collect dust on a harddrive until 2025 while there are people out there who could be enjoying these songs and actually want to move into the future with me would be such a waste! With the guidance and support by Jason Meinzer and the opportunities presented to artists in this day and age this seems like the perfect time to start building that Warmheart Society!

My Awakening to Adult ADHD

For years, my life felt like a puzzle, where pieces didn't fit quite right. I struggled with tasks that seemed simple for others, my mind a whirlwind of thoughts and distractions. It wasn't until someone randomly said to me you might have ADHD you know, since then when I have said I might have ADHD everyone say "hell yeah you have!! I may be paraphrasing there, I live in Essex, not Texas! 

The pieces began to fall into place, revealing a picture labelled "Adult ADHD." I decided to take my self to the Doctors, My GP with asking me a few questions he said, that although he wasn't a specialist (OBvs) hence the GP title ! He says he was almost certain that this was what it was.
ADHD isn't just a childhood condition; it walks silently into adulthood, often masked by societal expectations and personal denial. My journey started with confusion and misunderstanding, both by myself and medical professionals. The realization hit when I stumbled upon a community online, people who shared their stories, echoing my experiences and struggles.

The Personal Cost of ADHD
Relationships and ADHD: Navigating Through Turmoil
ADHD doesn't just affect the individual; it ripples through relationships, leaving chaos in its wake. My fiancée, the cornerstone of my support, left. The battle for my son became not just a legal fight but a quest for understanding and acceptance.

Self-Therapy Through Creativity
Music as a Form of Healing
In the midst of turmoil, I found solace in music. Writing and producing became a lifeline, a way to express the inexpressible.
Seeking Support: My GoFundMe Page for ADHD Treatment
The Importance of Community Support in Mental Health
Fees - What Does It Cost For ADHD Assessment & Treatments?
ADHD fees for full assessment & treatments. Highest quality consultation from initial assessment to on-going treatment…adhdclinic.co.uk

Now having had the appointment with my GP he has referred me to a clinic in London, this was 10 Months ago and no sign of the appointment, all the while I'm getting worse in a way that it is destressing me and those around me in an extreme way.

Due to me not being untreated and the hanging on since the referral, unable to make bills let alone go private to get me back on the track I thought that I would see if the community would help get me out of this ever deeper hole not seeing a way out.






With this worsening situation, personally and professionally, with this, a light at the end of the tunnel. I also plan to return the money to donors once I get myself back on my feet again.

Treatment for ADHD is a journey, one that is often expensive and fraught with obstacles. I've turned to the community for support, setting up a GoFundMe page in hopes of finding the resources to manage my ADHD effectively.

Behind the Music: Crafting "Rise Above"

Introduction

Join us on a journey of empowerment and triumph as we delve into the creation and essence of "Rise Above." This electrifying anthem is a celebration of inner strength and resilience, capturing the exhilarating journey of self-discovery and empowerment. From its inception to its explosive production, witness the evolution of a song that inspires listeners to break free from the chains of doubt and soar to new heights.

Inception

"Rise Above" emerges from the depths of adversity, a testament to the songwriter's journey of self-discovery and empowerment. Inspired by personal experiences of overcoming obstacles and embracing inner strength, the song serves as a rallying cry for anyone who has ever felt trapped by doubt or despair. With each verse and chorus, they invite listeners to join them on a journey of transformation, where darkness gives way to light and fear is replaced by courage.

Lyricism

The lyrics of "Rise Above" paint a vivid portrait of resilience and determination. From the empowering verses to the anthemic chorus, every word resonates with raw emotion and unwavering conviction. The imagery of breaking through the clouds and soaring high evokes a palpable sense of liberation, while the recurring motif of rising above adversity symbolizes the triumph of the human spirit. Through poetic introspection, the songwriter invites listeners to embrace their inner strength and seize their destiny.

Melodic Alchemy

The melody of "Rise Above" is a symphony of energy and empowerment, crafted with precision to mirror the euphoric journey of self-discovery. The pulsating beats and uplifting melodies create a dynamic soundscape that propels listeners to new heights of exhilaration. With each drop and build-up, the music builds to a crescendo of liberation, offering solace and redemption in the face of doubt and despair.

Production

In the studio, "Rise Above" undergoes a metamorphosis, evolving from a mere concept into a fully-realized sonic powerhouse. Collaborating with musicians and producers, the songwriter meticulously crafts each layer of instrumentation, infusing the music with depth and texture. From the powerful EDM drops to the atmospheric breakdowns, every element is carefully orchestrated to enhance the song's thematic resonance and evoke an immersive listening experience.

Conclusion

"Rise Above" stands as a testament to the indomitable power of the human spirit and the transformative potential of music. Through its electrifying lyricism, uplifting melody, and explosive production, it invites listeners to embark on a journey of self-discovery and empowerment. As the final notes fade into the ether, the echoes of this triumphant anthem linger, a reminder that with courage and determination, anything is possible.

With "Rise Above," the songwriter has crafted a captivating piece of music that resonates with listeners on a deeply emotional level. May this exploration enrich your appreciation of the song and inspire you to embrace your own journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

"Backroads" is a song that journeys through the echoes of the past, carried on the dust and wind of memories. As th3scr1b3, I’ve always believed that music isn’t just an outlet for expression—it’s a way to confront the complexities of life, to turn the intangible into something you can feel and understand. In this track, I explore the deep emotional landscape of regret, nostalgia, and the haunting nature of lost opportunities.

The song's lyrics reflect a universal experience: the tension between where we are and where we’ve been. "Every time a twist, echoes of laughter, whispers of old dreams / They’re in my rearview mirror"—these words capture that paradox of moving forward while being constantly pulled back by the past. The backroads in the song symbolize the detours of life, the places where we linger on what could have been, but are forced to keep moving, even when the weight of regret feels overwhelming.

"Backroads" isn’t just a song about loss—it’s a meditation on memory, on the way we carry the weight of our choices. "Regret's a heavy load, a burden on my soul" speaks to the burden of living with decisions that can’t be undone, yet the song also leaves space for hope. The narrator is searching for a sign, a way to make peace with the past, to understand it. "On these backroads of regret, I’m searching for a sign / A way to turn back time, to the days when you were mine" reflects that longing for things to be different, while acknowledging that those days are gone.

Musically, "Backroads" blends th3scr1b3's freestyle roots with a reflective, melancholic beat that carries the emotional weight of the lyrics. The sound evolves with each twist in the song, like the winding roads it describes, building tension and release as the narrative unfolds. The collaboration with producers elevates the emotional atmosphere, ensuring that every turn, every mile, feels both personal and universal.

The song builds to a poignant realization: "Each mile marker passes, like pages in a book / A chapter closed, forever." In these final lines, the journey ends—not in resolution, but in the acceptance of what has been lost, and the understanding that the past, though haunting, is a part of who we are. "Backroads" is about navigating the emotional terrain of regret while finding a path forward, even when it seems like the road behind us is the only place we can go.
