Bitcoin to the 100. It is my life.

In 2018, underground artist Nuri began crafting "The Bitcoin Song" to commemorate Bitcoin's upcoming 10th anniversary. He wanted to capture the rebellious essence of cryptocurrency, but the song wasn't fully realized until 2023. That year, as the global economic landscape grew more uncertain, Nuri felt the time was right. Working under the production company we named Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers Social Club, which also launched an NFT collection with over 9,000 versions of the track, he perfected "Bitcoin XV 2024" in time for Bitcoin’s 15th anniversary on January 3rd, 2024. The song opens with a bold proclamation of "Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers," signaling the cryptocurrency’s rise from its genesis in 2009 to a revolutionary financial force.

Nuri’s lyrics vividly address Bitcoin’s critics, portraying them as out-of-touch skeptics while celebrating Bitcoin's ability to empower the masses. He raps about flipping the financial script, mocking Wall Street insiders, and emphasizing Bitcoin’s value as fair money for the people. The chorus echoes this sentiment: "Bitcoin, like gold is rare; Bitcoin makes money fair." With references to icons like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and James Brown, Nuri connects Bitcoin’s financial revolution to broader struggles for justice. Through "Bitcoin XV 2024," both the song and the NFT collection stand as powerful symbols of Bitcoin’s enduring legacy, celebrating a movement that isn’t going anywhere.

Nuri’s groundbreaking NFT project, launched under the Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers production company, pushed the boundaries of digital art and music in a way that had never been done before. With over 9,000 unique versions of "The Bitcoin Song," the project was designed to commemorate Bitcoin’s 15th anniversary in a monumental fashion. Each NFT version features variations in verses, choruses, beats, and production layers, creating an extensive, one-of-a-kind collection. No other artist had ever created so many distinct versions of a single song, making the project a trailblazer in the NFT space. This innovative concept not only allows fans to own a piece of Bitcoin’s legacy but also personalized the experience by offering an exclusive version for each NFT holder. By combining cutting-edge technology with the revolutionary ethos of cryptocurrency, Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers Social Club NFT collection is redefining how music is experienced, shared, and monetized in the digital age.

At first, I was aiming to make a remix, but then we both realized this song asked for much more. We kept searching for the right balance. Finally, the up-and-coming lyricist and MC Atomic the Don, whose raps you can hear in the second verse, added a new dimension to the entire concept of this beautiful, cautious, and modern song. 

Thus, we are blending all of our 3 worlds - Gnoia, Atomic and Fenix. We hope "Psyche" will serve you for many years to come with its message, emotions, and deep sound. Enjoy.

A ghostly waltz for the walking wounded, *"Save Yourself"* is Gypsylost’s venom-laced lullaby to codependency, where her signature tarot-card whimsy collides with the brutal reality of love as a bloodsport. The track unfolds like a séance gone wrong—mournful piano keys dissolve into industrial snarls as her voice shifts between haunted-child whispers and the guttural growl of something far older. Lyrics like *"I’ll light your candles if you dig my grave"* aren’t metaphors; they’re autopsy reports from relationships where she played both savior and sacrifice.  

This song was scrawled in the margins of a stolen motel Bible at 3AM, somewhere between Nashville’s neon glow and the Carolina backroads. Gypsylost wrote it after realizing every person she’d ever resurrected had only wanted her bones for their altar. The production mirrors that revelation—church-choir harmonies warp into static, like a radio losing signal mid-prayer. It’s not a breakup song. It’s an exorcism. Press play if you’re ready to watch the pyre consume what you once swore you’d die for.

I saw a city steeped in endless calm,  
Shattered by time that stretches without end.  
There, wires hum beneath the wind’s wild psalm,  
And windows stare, blind to the void they tend.  

Once, people built their world with dreams of might,  
To rule o’er all that is, their grand design.  
But now their flame is quenched, their reason slight,  
Leaving an echo in the skies’ loud whine.  

Sand and ash weave patterns in the air,  
Footsteps of the past drown in silence deep.  
What did we seek in our mad, fervent prayer?  
Why did we raise these walls so high and steep?  

And in this world where only shadows roam,  
Nature whispers: "All shall return to loam."

"U.(S.AD)" by Mr.FLEN is a hard-hitting critique of America's current socio-political landscape. This grime-influenced track takes listeners on a journey through economic struggles, political disillusionment, and the everyday reality of the working class. Mr.FLEN tackles major issues like skyrocketing inflation, the broken healthcare system, and the growing wealth gap, all while delivering sharp, biting lyrics that leave nothing off the table.

With powerful imagery and relentless flow, Mr.FLEN points fingers at the bipartisan blame game in Washington, where both Democrats and Republicans are too wrapped up in their own power plays to address the real issues affecting Americans. The chorus highlights the frustration felt by many: the dollar’s value plummeting, politicians moving too slow, and ordinary people bearing the brunt of these failures.

In his second verse, Mr.FLEN further exposes the divide between Wall Street's booming profits and Main Street's pain, where families are struggling just to survive while banks and corporations thrive. The interlude is a reflective moment, calling out the repetitive nature of political games and demanding real change, urging listeners to rise up against complacency.

The final verse shifts focus to the climate crisis, rising crime, and the hollow narratives pushed by mainstream media, reinforcing the idea that the true fight lies in the hands of everyday people. Mr.FLEN’s clever wordplay and grim outlook provide a gritty yet truthful commentary on the state of the nation, with a clear call for action by the track’s conclusion.

"U.(S.AD)" is more than just a song—it's a raw depiction of America’s current struggles, wrapped in gritty grime beats and relentless bars that refuse to let the listener stay complacent. The title itself reflects the sadness of the state of the U.S. (United States), a nation that once stood tall, now battling deep fractures within.

Perfect for fans of politically charged music like Dave or Skepta, Mr.FLEN gives a voice to the voiceless, calling out the systems in power that need to be held accountable.

The Story:

"Dive" was written, recorded, produced, mixed and mastered by Mikey Maramag (Blackbird Blackbird) in Montréal, Canada, circa March 2024. Lyrics by Mikey Maramag.

Feelings can crystallize so deeply & intensely that at first it feels like you are diving into a vast sea of love, or an 'ocean of love', as the lyrics portray in the second verse (one of my personal favorite parts of any song I've ever done).

The intro hook "Don't worry, I'll catch you if you fall", foreshadows the drama of the second chorus, and refers to the initial feeling of uncertainty of the start of a relationship. 

Diving straight in to something real, with barely any time to test the waters is scary at first, but sometimes love comes in a rush of moments and happens so fast that it takes over your entire world in no time at all. 

Throughout the song I wanted to play around with space. The intro starts dry and trots along, kind of symbolizing where I was at in life & reflecting on the difficulty I had in finding a love that wasn't toxic or superficial. 

Then the gentle guitar plucks come in and glue things together playfully, sparking an ambition & building curiosity. Only through self-care and bettering myself was I able to be alone and content with myself, which is also what happened right before I met my true love, and gave me fortitude & strength to accept this love.

There is also a kind of kinophobia, or fear of open spaces (which I personally suffer from sometimes) that I wanted to address in structure and feel of the song. In contrast to this feeling, love bridges distances, brings people closer, and acts like a warm light or radiance, like something familiar--something that feels like home. Hopefully the song can do this for you as well.

The buildup right before the drop into the synth-driven, abyssal ocean that is the chorus, I wanted it to feel like the listener is catching their breath & getting ready to 'Dive' in!

Meeting your true love can feel like a religious experience, a moment of awe, or an instant cure-all for the nihilistic loneliness & dystopia of modern dating life. But there are always challenges in a relationship or partnership, and I wanted to express the mutual feeling of being there for each other to catch each other, in case either of us falls down, we'll help each other get back up.

I guess I just thought, why not just put all these different conflicting emotions of love together and write a song about it. Dive is what I came up with. I hope it can help others find both true love and SELF-LOVE, and regardless of what they are going through I'm happy to have it out in the world & hope you enjoy! :)

Love,
Mikey

In the realm of my tumultuous love affair with the music industry, I am trying to paint a vivid picture through the metaphor of a romantic relationship and drug addiction. Picking up the industry from its metaphorical class, armed with roses and candy symbolizing my passion and dedication, my optimism is shattered when I discover the industry kissing another man, representing the betrayals and challenges I faces. The chorus, "I'll Never Learn," becomes a poignant mantra echoing the cyclic nature of my struggles. The lyrics delve into the paradox of the industry, likening it to a demanding partner that never reciprocates as much as it takes. I am caught in the addictive cycle, narrating the highs and lows, using vivid imagery and wordplay to convey the complexities of my relationship. The story unfolds as I grapple with the toll it takes on my mental well-being, resorting to substances as a coping mechanism. Despite the hardships, the allure of the music industry persists, leaving me ensnared in a cycle of addiction and creative passion, ultimately resigning myself to the perpetual refrain of "I'll Never Learn."

Her contribution to The Culture Tape Vol 1, "Unlimited Dreams," is an empowering rock anthem that encapsulates her message of relentless pursuit of one's dreams, irrespective of the obstacles, expectations, or labels faced. Produced by Grammy-winning Rodney "Darkchild" Jerkins, the track emphasizes Caly's commitment to inspiring hope and bravery.

I MANIFEST, from Symbolik's Breadth Of Existence album, is an offering of ancient cultural expression, observational commentary, and Hip Hop poetry. Inspired by the Kemetic tree of life research and a community call to depict and represent the balance that exists between the cosmic, spirittual and Geb the physical.

I MANIFEST is the result of an international collaboration with Symbolik (Toronto, Canada) and Webber from Yin Sang (Beijing, China), and represents the universal nature of Hip Hop.

I MANIFEST was originally released in a limited capacity in 2007, and reflects the influence of the era that is known as "True School" Hip Hop, where lyricism, deeper meanings and social impact where core to the Hip Hop form.

The artist Symbolik gained experience, knowledge and a sense of self from the global Hip Hop movement. While he has worked in the media/interactive media and communications space, and went on to earn his BFA and Masters in Fine Arts and Interactive Production, Symbolik always considered Hip Hop his first and most foundational training ground.

Symbolik believes that music, art and social empowerment onchain is an amazing new way to express, support and vote for what we, love and want to see more of in the world. Symbolik is excited to release I MANIFEST on Sound.xyz and is confident this collectible will look and sound great in your wallet!

Velvet Meadow brings a new FUNKY flare to his sound with new single "Its My Fault". During the writing phase of this track, Heironimus wanted to experiment with writing something with some groove and soul into it. The track was written in his rented out room in St Augustine Florida shortly after gaining inspiration from some of vintage R&B soul records he picked up from a nearby flea market. Upon release, it has become a staple in his discography gaining over 4k streams its first week, with a continuous climb. 

"I wanted to write something that is a little out of my comfort zone. I wanted something more upbeat, and more upfront strong vocals with a little cheekiness to it. Its got to be one of my favorite pop tunes I have written. I just kind of jumped into the deep with it writing, and production wise. My favorite aspect of it is the counter melody in the chorus thing spouting its my fault. I also love the ending with the synthesizers getting super trippy. I am a huge synth head, always will be. I was super stoked it did so well, as I thought it would be a lot more niche in the psych pop world than it is." Kris Heironimus

Thank you to everyone supporting the project. It means the world to me I have so many supporters and all around groovy people in this community. You guys are the backbone of this project. If you are new to the project, welcome to the Meadow. <3

Llévame is rooted in one of the most intensely personal and transformative experiences of my life. During a trip to Amsterdam with a close friend, the city’s energy and the effects of magic mushrooms brought us closer in every possible way. The connection was wild, raw, and unapologetically physical. We completely surrendered to the moment, exploring each other with no reservations, letting go of everything but the sensations we shared.

The lyrics reflect that passion—lines like “Hasta el fondo de tu ser” aren’t just poetic. They’re a reflection of how deeply we connected, both physically and emotionally. With every thrust, her body responded, and the more I pushed, the more she let go, completely giving in to the moment. Each time we came together, her body unable to contain the intensity. The experience was mutual—an exchange of raw pleasure and connection. We lost ourselves in it, pushing the boundaries of what we thought possible.

The video blends reality with surreal elements, mirroring the hallucinatory state we were in. Just like the experience, it’s a mix of the real and the dreamlike, taking the viewer through that journey of physical and emotional surrender. It’s a visual and auditory trip that reflects the raw essence of what happened that night.

ABOUT SPIRIT AWAY

Spirit Away is about the self-reflection that occurs post-relationship.

In this case, it’s about me looking in the mirror, seeing the crows feet around my eyes, a few gray hairs, and wondering, "Do I still have what it takes to pursue what I want in life or am I kidding myself?"

I imagine a lot of people go through this at some point in life, perhaps multiple times. Spirit Away is simply me acknowledging when those feelings arise. If someone listens to it and can relate, at least they’ll know they aren’t alone.


SOME EXCERPTS

“Who is this? Looking back at me?
The creases in his eyes try not to lie
but can’t help talking through the steam and
he knows talk is cheap."

It’s sobering when I realize that while I’ve put countless reps into pursuing what I want in life, there’s still plenty of times when I’ve been all talk. I know that the solution is in the reps, so that when the opportunities (or luck, however you want to frame it) come along, I’ll be prepared for them, but I’m also 40 years old. As much as I believe age is simply a number, there’s a different level of self-doubt that surfaces as I get older. It’s odd, like simultaneously living between confidence with age and self-doubt with age.


“And he’s had love, but not the lasting kind.
Like a rolling stone, he has big dreams,
but can’t quite seem to see clearly that
the moss you gather’s fine."

I’ve come to realize the culmination of experiences I’ve had, both in love and life pursuits, are just those — experiences. Rather than viewing them as failures of where I should have turned left instead of right, I now try my best to view them as a stone that has gathered moss, but the moss is a defining feature of the stone, and what gives it character while on its journey.


“It’s like I’m waiting on everything I’m chasing
to come and spirit me away from here."

I used to live in Japan, and while many people know of the beautiful movie Spirited Away, it’s the concept of being spirited away that inspired me for this set of lyrics. I feel like the concept of someone vanishing and returning at a later time is a part of Japanese folk lore — enough to where there’s terminology for it, 神隠し (kami kakushi) — in a way that I haven’t seen in the United States. Indeed, the best translation seems to be spirited away. In the case of the lyrics, I’m trying to convey that it often feels like I’m waiting for something to happen, some magic spirit from my goals to take me where I want to go, and in doing so, have missed opportunities, either from a lack of putting in the reps or lack of being proactive.


OTHER INTERESTING NOTES

Spirit Away (as well as the whole EP) was co-produced by me (Mike Bass), Alara, and Steven LaFashia. This was my first time working with other producers, and enjoyed the process very much!

Spirit Away features an incredible singer-songwriter, musician, and friend, Emma Miller. The beautiful background/harmony vocals you hear that give the song another depth of life are done by Emma.

The Branches EP was recorded at Retro City Studios in Philadelphia, PA.

Spirit Away blends more into the indie-folk genre, which is new for me. The same goes for the EP as a whole, which has dream pop, indie folk, and even indie pop elements.

records.title: Black Water (with San Holo & Lizzy Land)

Description:
San Holo and I wrote the beat together, mostly around some piano parts that re recorded live. It had a few different toplines on it, but I sent it to Lizzy Land because I thought her tone would work perfectly for it. We were talking about imperfection and how to embrace that. Black Water itself represents a metaphor for the realisation that you can find most of the answers to life’s questions from looking inward rather than out.

"It was an amazing experience to work with musicians as talented as Daktyl and Lizzy Land! Getting to create with artists that I love is such an honor, and I'm so happy with how the song turned out." - San Holo

"Black Water is about having all the answers you need inside. In your darkest moments, when you feel alone without hope, there is this pool of infinite, eternal knowing that spills out in front of you. A mirror reflecting what you already know back to you.

Daktyl and I wrote “black water” while talking about expectations. The idea that perfect does and doesn’t exist. Like nature or the night sky. Imperfection is a human opinion and ultimately you hold the key to your own happiness.” - Lizzy Land

And I realized, we are all dead snowflakes.
And here and there, they are already lying,
Reminding us, of the frailty of this life.

They are born in the sky and fly.
Free and at liberty to live as they wish.
Having accelerated their run, they circle faster,
Like people, in the recklessness of gray days.

They will stop moving, touching the ground.
And they die... they die, one way or another...
Some will remain nothing, never waking up.
Others, something... But they won't be cried for either.

Children will sculpt fortresses and build slides.
Throw corpses of snowflakes, with frozen hands.
They will paint snowdrifts yellow, different lapdogs, Yorkies...
And the same children will touch them with frozen lips.

But winter will end, and sooner or later,
The janitors will rake up the snowflakes, ending their short life.
And so that in the spring, having become a dirty puddle,
They could turn back into dead snow in winter...

"No Company" is a rallying cry for people like us, who have had to dig deep and figure out a way to navigate through life.

"How am I to be creative? Nature knows only one answer to that: Through a child (the gift of love)." (Jung)

The next single from Spectres deals with the archetype of the Child, which Jung called "an image of both the irrecoverable past and an anticipation of future development." Furthermore, he wrote that "In every adult there lurks a child–an eternal child, something that is always becoming, is never completed, and calls for unceasing care, attention, and education. That is the part of the personality which wants to develop and become whole."

Comprising 13 experimental tracks produced over the last seven years, Spectres is the 28th release in my discography but my first ever completely solo full-length album. While working on this record, I delved deep into Jungian psychology, concepts from which became central to the project. All 13 tracks are named after archetypes—innate, universal forces that shape our experience of the world.

Spectres is also a visual art project. For each track, I crowd-sourced images associated with the corresponding archetype. These image collections were used to train bespoke Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), simulating the complex interplay between individual psyche and collective unconscious. A further GAN was trained on selected outputs from all the previous GANs, uniting the various archetypes to form an integrated Self.

By limiting the training time of these AI models, I found I could achieve results that mirrored the formation of archetypal symbols as I imagine them deep in our collective unconscious: elusive yet powerful forms emerging from abstract swirls of colour. From thousands of outputs, I selected and manually edited one per archetype to create unique artworks for each track. A collection of 144 further images from this project dropped under the title Spectral Shadows.

Ultimately, Spectres is more than a collection of WAVs and JPGs; it is a dialogue between the personal and the universal, a multidisciplinary exploration of the forces that connect us all. The album has taken me on a transformative seven-year journey through sound, imagery and psyche. In the process, individual and collective experience harmonise, casting a light into the profound depths of human interconnectedness.

Before its official release on 11/23, I'm rolling Spectres out across the web3 ecosystem, with drops on Sound, Zora, Rodeo, Lens and other emerging platforms. In a novel release structure, collectors of individual tracks gain instant access to stream the full album months before its official release. The goal is to push the limits of onchain interoperability to explore what a web3-native album release can look like in 2024.

For my genesis Sound drop it was important to stay true to the essence. I could’ve gone with another style of music but it was key for me to make history by sticking to the roots. When I first got into crypto in 2017, I noticed that the majority of the artists involved were in electronic music, a culture I was also a part of but I knew it would be an uphill battle to get Reggaeton recognition in the space. Fast-forward a few years and I accomplished everything I set out too in crypto/web3. (so far)

I made this song late 2021, I was on a hot streak knocking down about 3 records a night and “SOLTERA” was born. I needed a dope Reggaeton for the INFINXTE album and this was the one. The track is produced by two of my closest friends, Los Hitmen, a grammy-nominated production duo that have worked with heavyweights like J Balvin, Jay Wheeler, and De La Ghetto. I remember as soon as I sent the track I got a call back right away like “WTF DID YOU DO HERE?!” I knew right then we had a hit. 

The original artwork was crafted by one of my favorite artists from Spain, Diego (Paranoidme). I think one of the most exciting parts of my album is the diversity in collaborators, its completely organic and features artists from more than ten countries. Reggaeton was rejected in the mainstream for years and now its the voice of the youth all over Latin America, the Caribbean and people all over the world. Reggaeton pushes culture forward and I want to push it forward into web3.

Bela - 
A trip with friends will always be revealing. This song was born while I was on San Andrés island which is an island off the coast of Colombia known for its deep blue waters, warm weather and rich musical culture. This trip was about an escape, to get away from my thoughts and the people who appeared along the way made this trip something wonderful.

Xcelencia - 
I first learned about Bela promoting on Twitter which lead me to her OpenSea. As I went through her collection I noticed the versatility and knew right away she was a songwriter at heart. That definitely drew my attention since I worked on the publishing side of music for several years helping writers and producers. I collected one of the songs in the collection making it the first music NFT I purchased to support other Latin artists in the space.

We were talking about collaborating for some time and ISLA was the perfect song to start with. The Afrobeats inspired soundscape and the Rhodes driven chord progression set the tone for the song. This is one of those records where I effortlessly did my thing inspired by her writing and the production. This is the remix. 

🌴

Anatomía is the first single from Infinxte Side B. 

The infinite sessions totaled about 40 songs. There was no strategy or sound when I started working on the album. I didn't want it to be sonically cohesive - I didn't make it for critical acclaim. This decision gave me creative freedom and I evolved as a singer-songwriter. If you listen closely, you can tell.

The future of Latin music is free of industry expectations, trends and algorithms. It leans towards alternative, experimental and fusions. Anatomía is my version of that, it takes from all of my influences and brings them in full circle. ♾️

Ever since moving to Los Angeles I've had the pleasure of doing a bunch of sessions with talented vocalists. The process has taught me how to be comfortable in a room and make people feel ready to record, all while trying to be quick on my feet as a producer and catch a vibe with the artist I'm working with.

Over the past few months I've realized that most of the music I've made has been in sessions. And while I love vocal-driven music, I haven't really had the chance to sit back and do my own instrumental production experiments. When I look back on how I got started in music, so much of it was by myself sitting in a room twisting knobs and making odd sounds.

Honey is me taking a step back in that direction - it's a science experiment of a song that serves as my reminder to let go and have fun producing and to not take myself so seriously.

I wrote this song for my girlfriend back when she wasnt too sure if she wanted to be mine. Its funny because the reason she wasnt sold was because she thought I wasnt ready for it. 
 

This song was just a reminder, letting her know how devoted I actually am and how ready I actually was.

This one is for all of you who have been supporting me so far... it means the world!

These are the words I want to say when I float away and leave my body behind. 

Time dissipates when I am dancing. My movement encapsulates the interconnectedness of memory, instinct, emotion, and truth. But when the sweat dries and the clocks start up again, my identity can become distorted and blurred. Regret, guilt, fear, and loss flood my mind, ripping me away from the love that colors my life.

This is disassociating for me; I am no longer in control of my body, words, or feelings and I am a shell with empty eyes. My mind hovers and every conversation is empty. My loved ones feel abandoned while we are sitting right across from one another. I wrote these lyrics while fighting a dissociative episode and I managed to come back to myself through making my experience tangible and real with words and sound.

This song is a reclamation of myself. When I’m ready to become real again, patient love is always there to welcome me back home.

When I was in college I got ahold of The Chainsmokers’ managers’ e-mail address. They had just dropped a record called “Everybody Hates Me” and as a new producer on the scene I wanted to take a pass at remixing it. I figured the best case scenario would be The Chainsmokers noticing me and taking me on a world tour with them and the worst case would be no response. To my surprise, the stems were sitting in my inbox within the hour. For the first time in my life, I had a fully processed, industry-standard engineered vocal that I could do anything with. The possibilities were endless. 

I skipped class for a week and went back and forth on seven or eight different versions of the remix - and while I didn’t get the Chainsmokers to sign off on it, I did fall in love with a new process of making music. For the next few years I would wake up every morning, go to New Music Friday on Spotify, track down management e-mails on the artists’ Facebook “about” section and beg for stems. Over the years, I put out a bunch of remixes for various artists - but more importantly I slowly compiled high quality vocals that I could mess with in my spare time. To this day, that remains one of my preferred method of working on records with people; “Ball!” with Kevin George (which was my last sound drop) happened from him sending me an acapella and my imagination running with it.

At the time, I was paid for remixes with exposure - and I wouldn’t have had it any other way. People started listening to my music on Soundcloud for the first time and I started to meet my first music friends through that experience. A lot of them are still my friends today.

However, there are a slew of examples of remixes that came out that went on to perform better than the original song did. More times than not, the remixer is paid in either exposure (like me), or a one time buyout fee which is typically $250 or less for smaller artists. Most of the time, the remixers - who breathe new life into the record - see no upside in the event that the remix is a smash. These artists are also overlooked often and don’t get a chance to tell their musical stories.

The Glass House remixes is a 4 pack of my favorite reworks off my EP “Glass House”. Every remix came out incredible, and flipped my songs into a way I never saw coming.

The pack features artists who vary in Web3 experience - from vets like Clear Eyes and MSFT to newcomers like Veggi and Cudos, I’m stoked to present the first Daniel Allan Remix pack on Sound.

Welcome to Eternal Garden.

Eternal Garden follows the story of Caius, an angel cast out of heaven by the goddess Flora, tasked with a mission to terraform a now desolate and uninhabitable earth. Though his mission was successful, he broke the singular rule necessary for an angel’s survival. Caius falls in love with an earthly being, later revealed to be a centuries old shapeshifter, and falls into a deep slumber. Locked in a daydream, he relives the memories of a thousand men, unlocking the secrets of the human condition as he experiences love, heartbreak, and resentment over and over again. He awakens to a world on fire and stripped of his angelic blessing. To reclaim his power and fulfill his promise, Caius embarks on a treacherous journey to the Eternal Garden - a portal between Heaven and Earth, and the source of their vitality. 

7 Songs, 7 Visuals, 7 Forbidden Fruits, 700 Editions.

Read more at: www.eternal-garden.xyz

Hurricane is a perfect rendition of the sound we always envisioned for Koastle. It started with a DM after I (Andy) found Talia Rose on my Discover Weekly Spotify playlist while she had only 1,000 monthly listeners. Fun fact is that Talia actually quit music around the time I reached out, she hadn't made any new music for about a year but was coincidentally visiting LA to visit her girlfriend who was in the area at the time. So after working with a publishing label that was treating me like I was a slave, I got stuck in form and this idea that songwriting has to be one way, I took some time to heal because I really couldn’t write for months. To help, I decided to ride my bike to clear my head, and one day I envisioned myself rapping a verse on the L.A. River. And that’s how “Joyride” came to life. 

“Joyride” is an evolving practice of free verses that are straight to it. No form, just me and me philosophies in bars. It’s a meditation, it’s short bits of me, it’s whatever you want to make it. An opportunity to just allow myself to ride the beat. To create these verses, I would start with a beat I love, rap on it and then send the accapella to Kaui to create something new out of it.

“Culture”, this first offering/verse off of “Joyride” came to me after rapping on Kaytranada’s production. I wrote the verse in a nite and immediately knew I didn’t want to add much else to it. I am very lyrical and I am realizing, sometimes one verse is enough. Sometimes keeping it simple is all you need. Sometimes just riding your own path is what I have to do. 

So this year as I’m riding my path, I guess I’m using this “Joyride” as an exercise in getting back to me, getting out of my way, sticking to my journey, continuing to create with bro Kaui who has been working with me for years, I’m really excited for how this ride will take me to more paths.  Next up “Showtime”

What if you could meet your past or future self across space and time. What might you advise, observe, affirm, or say to yourself ?

One truth I would reveal to my past self is: 
you will use your voice and your journal entries will become poems, stories will become speeches, and songs will spring forth into the world to become your legacy. 

“Infinite” is a dance between my past, present, and future self. If we see more limitlessly we find that time is in fact not short, time is abundant as well, life is the longest dance we will ever know.   

The world is what it is, for better or worse because people shaped it so, that being said, I believe we are in an everlasting cycle of co-creation with the universe. “Infinite” asks us to get on the dancefloor ( a metaphor for life) and tap in with self and one another to create the world we want to live in and leave behind for future  generations. 

Art imitates life and life imitates art. Dreams are sacred and I believe we don’t quit until we’ve lived each one.

Everyday I reaffirm to present self that I am surrounded by supportive community, I can step out of my way and let the blessings flow into my life. 
Breathe now look up, look within, and look how far we’ve come. 

If I met my future self, I would encourage her to  continue to enjoy the fruits of her labor and to keep finding ways to honor all the people she has encountered along the way, they have  all mattered.

I am inspired daily and have so much love for so many of you in ways that don’t even belong to me🙏🏾

"This Holiday" is a festive anthem that captures the enchanting spirit of the winter season. The lyrics paint a vivid picture of a winter wonderland, with snow falling gently, lights illuminating the surroundings, and a carriage ride through the dreamlike scenery. Th3scr1b3 expresses a deep appreciation for the magical blend between the tangible reality and the cognitive enchantment of the holiday season.

The heart of the song lies in the th3scr1b3's desire to perpetuate the magical scene, encapsulating it forever in the canvas of their mind and design. The ambiance is further enriched by the sight of children in winter coats, creating a sense of innocence and joy. The lyrics celebrate the magic of the holiday season, emphasizing the importance of creating moments of enchantment and wonder.

As the narrative unfolds, the singer invites a shared experience of magic-making. The act is not only for the couple but extends to everyone touched by the love and warmth of the season. The mention of mistletoe, St. Nick, and the vibrant colors in the dark evokes a sense of tradition and the timeless allure of the holidays.

The chorus becomes a joyful declaration, urging a collective effort to make magic this holiday season. It's a call to embrace the brightness, warmth, and love that the season brings. The lyrics encourage a sense of togetherness, assuring that the magic lies in the shared experience of the glow, the laughter, and the love that permeates the air during this special time.

"This Holiday" is a jubilant celebration of the magic that can be found in shared moments, love, and the timeless joy of the holiday season.

"Drive!" stands as the fourth single from my latest EP, "Cold River," which I unveiled in March of this year. Reflecting on the journey from the song's inception to its release in March and now as it finds a home on Sound, it's a poignant experience. The track delves into my struggles with addiction, a subject that has undergone significant evolution since its creation. Although I've now reached almost five months of sobriety from both alcohol and substances, revisiting these themes remains a humbling reminder.

Amidst the changes, I've discovered a sense of peace and harmony on my ongoing journey. I hope that, as I release this project for the second time, some of you can find resonance in the shared experience. Music possesses a timeless quality, prompting me to reconsider promoting these tracks again. There are listeners out there who may be encountering them for the first time, and to them, it's a novel experience. The essence of art and storytelling lies in perpetual promotion—always strive to share your authentic narrative with kindness and respect for yourself and others. Trust that things will fall into place organically.

"Drive!" holds a special place among the tracks I've crafted; it's one of my personal favorites. The vibe of cruising around while immersed in its melodies sends shivers down my spine.

Enjoy!

It’s not surprising that an artist who is as deeply influenced by Prince as Morris Mills would chafe at the genre limits and expectations imposed on black artists by the music industry. Prince used his determination and talent to force fans and music executives to rethink the way that they viewed and marketed what would be normally labeled as R&B. Those racialized labels and genres became clay in Prince’s hands that he reworked into the form of his choosing.

Mills finds himself pushing against the same constraints with his latest album, The Dawn, a record that is a Princely cauldron of funk, rock, punk, R&B with a dash of hip-hop. The Dawn shares an additional commonality with much of Prince’s work, in that Mills’ art resides comfortably at the intersection between the sacred and the worldly.

In the hushed corridors of emotion, where heartbreak echoes and love's remnants linger, emerges a haunting melody that weaves through the tapestry of pain and healing. "Left Me All Alone" is more than a song; it's a soulful expedition into the depths of vulnerability, capturing the raw essence of a shattered heart.

“Verte” is a song that holds a special place in my heart. It was born from one of the most challenging moments in my life—a relationship that ended not because we wanted it to, but because of a clash that involved my family. Sometimes, love and relationships face tests that push us beyond our limits, and “Verte” reflects the longing, the regret, and the desperate desire to make things right.

When you go from sharing every moment with someone to waking up without them, it’s like a piece of you is missing. This song came to me during one of those sleepless nights, the ones where all you can think about is the person you love. Even my pet dragon, Kira, felt the absence and would often look for her. It’s moments like those that inspired the raw emotion behind this track.

I hope this song resonates with you, especially if you’ve ever loved and lost. It’s about wanting a second chance, about realizing our mistakes, and hoping that maybe, just maybe, it’s not too late.

I wrote this when I was a kid, 21 maybe. The acoustic is tuned to a D Tuning. We recorded it in '77 at John Stewart's Studio in Edington, ME, out on Rt. 9 heading east out of Bangor. John ran the board. It was an 8 track setup. 

Bob Elie came in on drums and brought a Bass player friend of his from Lewiston. We can't remember who he was. A serious drag as he did a great job and I'd love to give him credit. Harry King came in to play keys but not on this track. Mark 'Guitar' Miller played electric guitar and slide but was not there for the beds. He came in a couple weeks later to put down his tracks.

I did the mix with John and have been tortured by it for 45 years till technology opened the door to separate the tracks so I could isolate the vocal and drop it into the mix properly. The vocal was always too loud. I was also able to clean up the Bass and add a little snap to the Drums. 

All in all it's a solid track and it's a great relief to get it out there after 47 years. It couldn't be better, frankly. It was done and performed organically, with real emotion and purpose and was written by a kid who's whole life was in front of him and he was working out how he was gonna live it . .

Like most of my releases up to this point, I initially started Forager over a year before its release. According to a backup project file, I started it on November 2, 2022 (The day that FTX began to collapse, funny enough) - At the time, I was temporarily living in LA and working remotely for a web3 gaming project based in Saigon, Vietnam, that would soon let me go by the end of that month. It was a volatile period of my life for more personal reasons as well. None of this has anything to do with Forager, though- I can't say I drew inspiration from that chaos since I was actually focused on finishing my downtempo album Relics. Forager was probably just a demo I made on a whim, that really took shape in the Spring of this year. I just find that^ context interesting, looking back on it a year later...

Stylistically, Bonobo was a primary reference in the making of Forager, especially the song "Bambro Koyo Ganda." CloZee is another artist who was more inspiring to me when I was focused on world bass music, but Forager is proof that her influence persists even as I've pivoted to more club-focused styles this year, as it's built around a kalimba loop from one of her sample packs. 

So not only does Forager perfectly encapsulate my stylistic evolution by combining a 4-to-the-floor groove with a broken beat and a bass lead in the final drop, it also represents a shift in how* I produce music-- By embracing the art of sampling and rejecting the notion that I need to synthesize or program every sound and loop myself. This shift has unlocked an extraordinary amount of productivity and has helped me create my best songs yet that are still authentic to the Bastion sound. However, I did create the bass lead and wrote the strings and bass line as well. Another combo of old and new techniques, blending seamlessly into a Bastion original.

Forager is also special because it is the first track I'm minting on Sound.xyz! Which is very exciting. I firmly believe in the potential for web3 to help "re-price" music (the most undervalued art form today, relative to its impact on people and our society), hopefully making its creation a more reliable source of income for talented, professional musicians and artists in the years to come. By supporting this release, you are helping to make that future a reality. Thank you. 

~ Bastion

"My artist name is GAENDE, a French man who spent most of his life in Senegal, a place that became my second home. During my time in Senegal, I earned the nickname 'GAENDE,' which means 'LION' in the local language, Wolof. This nickname carries with it the strength and power of the lion, and it has inspired my first album, 'ROAR,' which serves as the embodiment of that primal energy."

The Story:
"ROAR" takes listeners on a transformative journey, from the very first track, "Inhale," to the closing note of "Exhale." It's a story of self-discovery, inner strength, and emotional catharsis.

Inhale: Picture yourself taking a deep breath, inhaling life itself. Each inhale is a moment of vitality, a reminder of the precious gift of existence. The track pulsates with a rhythmic intensity, reflecting the heartbeat of life.

Metamorphosis: As you continue to inhale deeply, you begin to feel a transformation within. Your heart races, and the world seems to grow louder. Yet, in this chaos, you strive for inner calm and focus, symbolized by a captivating metamorphosis in the music.

Rush: The noise around you gradually recedes, and your heartbeat grows softer. Rush of dopamine arrives as you delve deeper into your inner power. The music builds like a powershot, representing your inner strength.

Ignited Passion: With each passing moment, your passion ignites like a wildfire. The world blurs around you as you lose yourself in this powerful surge. The music reflects the frenzy of emotions, the racing heartbeat, and the chaotic beauty of passion.

ROAR (Title Track): This is the climax of your journey. Your inner fire roars to life, and you unleash all the love and hate within you. The music is intense, resonating with the raw power of your emotions, and it culminates in a thunderous chorus that echoes your ROAR.

Submerged: After the emotional explosion, you find yourself submerged in a sea of emotions. It's a moment of relief and change, as though you are shredding a heavy burden.

Solitude: In the aftermath, you discover a sense of blessed solitude. Deep within yourself, you find a tranquil place where calm and power coexist. The music reflects this inner sanctuary, enveloping you in a meditative and introspective aura.

Exhale: Finally, it's time to exhale and return to the world. As you release your breath, you appreciate the moment before beginning the cycle anew. The closing track embodies this sense of closure and renewal.

Introducing my latest track, a raw and unfiltered expression of the frustration and disillusionment that often accompanies the military experience. Crafted from the depths of my own struggles, this song is a reflection of the harsh realities faced by veterans who risk their lives for causes they may not fully understand or support.

The lyrics delve into the challenges of military life – the mental strain, the emotional toll, and the lack of support once the service is completed. It's a narrative born from my own journey, where I found myself homeless for two years in my car, all while trying to pursue an education and music career.

The inspiration behind this track goes beyond personal experience. It's a call to shed light on the thousands of veterans facing similar struggles, if not worse. The systemic issues within the system often leave those who served feeling neglected and abandoned.

The photo accompanying the track features my mom, a veteran who has experienced homelessness throughout my life. Her story, like many others, serves as a poignant reminder of the challenges that persist even after service. Despite her hardships, she remains resilient, choosing her path and doing well.

This song is more than just a personal release; it's a plea for awareness and empathy. Let's reflect on the impact of sending our children into wars on foreign lands and strive for a system that genuinely cares for those who have sacrificed so much.

Album "Meridian 68" is a unique album by the Polish-Ukrainian band Dagadana, which combines four cultures: Polish, Ukrainian, Mongolian, and Chinese. On the album, the group turns to fresh interpretations of timeless folk music pieces, which sound like a unique fusion of genres, mixing jazz, ethno, and electronics.

The album includes traditional songs from various regions of Poland, Ukrainian and Lemko folk songs, Mongolian poetry that can be heard here, as well as one unique song recorded in Chinese together with the Mongolian-Chinese band North Lab. "Meridian 68" was nominated for the "Fryderyk" award in the Album of the Year: Roots Music category.

Dagadana band has been brilliantly combining elements ofUkrainian and Polish culture through jazz, electronica or world music for fifteen years. It was founded in 2008 by Daga Gregorowicz (Poland) and Dana Vynnytska (Ukraine). Today, Dagadana is already a quartet, sometimes expanding to include a brass section and even a symphony orchestra. Dagadana was the only band from Poland and Ukraine to play at one of the world's biggest music festivals in 2019 - thelegendary Glastonbury Festival in the UK. Among others, theAmerican National Geographic wrote about it. The group hastoured in more than 30 countries, including the largest festivalin South America and a number of tours in China. Dagadana hasso far played on a raft, in a mine and even in the desert.

Tracy, with eyes like Parisian twilight and hair the color of a moonlit Seine, knew love's sweet song all too well. She met Etienne, a sculptor with calloused hands and a heart full of dreams, under the shadow of the Eiffel Tower. Their love story unfolded like a Monet painting, filled with stolen kisses by the Seine, whispered secrets in hidden cafes, and laughter echoing in the Louvre's grand halls.

He carved her name into his latest sculpture, a masterpiece showcasing the fragility and strength of the human heart. Tracy saw her own reflection in its curves, her love for him etched in stone. They dreamed of a life intertwined, a future painted in vibrant hues of shared passions.

But fate, a fickle artist, had other plans. Etienne, yearning to hone his craft, received a prestigious residency in Rome. Tears, bitterer than winter rain, fell as they said goodbye. Promises of unwavering love clung to the air, a fragile bridge across the miles.

Days turned into weeks, then months. Letters, once passionate and frequent, became sporadic, then silent. The ache in Tracy's heart deepened with each unanswered call, each empty message box. Rumors drifted across the ocean, whispers of a new muse in Rome, a fiery Italian sculptor captivating Etienne's soul.

Tracy clung to hope, a wilting flower reaching for the sun. The city of love mocked her with its romantic whispers, every corner echoing with memories of stolen kisses and whispered dreams. She channeled her pain into her art, painting portraits drenched in longing, landscapes reflecting the turmoil within.

One rainy afternoon, a package arrived. Inside, nestled in velvet, lay a delicate sculpture—a single feather, carved with exquisite detail. On it, a inscription: "Though love may change, its echo remains." The feather, fragile yet enduring, became a symbol of her shattered dreams and resilient spirit.

Tracy refused to be defined by heartbreak. She poured her experiences into her art, creating pieces that resonated with raw emotion and quiet strength. Her exhibitions drew crowds, her story whispered amidst the brushstrokes. Slowly, the ache in her heart dulled, replaced by a bittersweet acceptance.

Years later, a familiar aroma of Parisian rain wafted through her studio. Turning, Tracy saw Etienne, older, weathered, but with eyes that still held a flicker of their shared past. He spoke of love lost and lessons learned, of Rome's fire fading to embers.

Their conversation, like a familiar melody played in a minor key, held a melancholic beauty. They acknowledged the echoes of their love, its lingering presence shaping who they had become. They parted ways, two souls forever intertwined, yet moving on separate paths.

Tracy continued to paint, her art still tinged with the memory of lost love, but now imbued with an undercurrent of hope. For she had learned that even the most beautiful songs can turn bittersweet, their echoes guiding us towards new beginnings. The city of love, once a painful reminder, became a testament to her resilience, a canvas on which she painted her own story of heartbreak and healing.

The day 'Colours Dancing' was born, was a day of great introspection. Part of that process was mind mapping who I am and eventually what I wanted "OmegaKid" to reflect back into the world. Duality was the overriding theme - the concept that at any given time thousands of the most nightmarish situations and are occurring juxtaposed by thousands of miraculous situations. It fascinated me how the human experience is so individual, yet collective at the same time.

The first part of Rats(slash)Lovers explores the concept, that as extreme wealth inequality continues to rise exponentially, our place in society (as represented by the rat) has become a resource for the super wealthy/powerful to use indiscriminately, without accountability or real justice.

"Galvanise your voice" for you are human. You are allowed joy, space, time. The very fact that you exist and are conscious is incredible. Experience life, make positive changes every day, challenge yourself and those around you. "Your voice is one of many". There is power in community.

Conversely, is the story of the two lovers at the end of the song. "And both for the first time, Finding passion and fire." There is a tumult of emotion, but they are having a real experience, which we may feel we often have to deny due to the socio-economic burden placed on every single one of us. But in this moment, falling in love, you escape everything. There is colour in the world, optimism, hope and nothing else but the person standing in front of you.

I generated the art using midjourney to reflect this juxtaposition. This to me was the example of extreme contrast that will literally be going on consistently every second, of every day. It is both haunting and beautiful.

The air hummed with anticipation, a melody composed of laughter echoing through the cobbled streets and the rhythmic clatter of footsteps. Tonight, the House of Whispers hosted its annual Masquerade Ball, an event where reality dissolved and dreams danced with shadows.

Elara, her mask a shimmering mosaic of starlight, adjusted the intricate clockwork gears hidden beneath its surface. Tonight, she wasn't just a guest, but the architect of the night's magic. Her mechanical butterflies, each a symphony of gears and moonlight, fluttered amongst the guests, whispering secrets and igniting conversations.

A masked figure, his cloak swirling like midnight smoke, approached Elara. "The Clockwork Queen," he murmured, his voice a low rumble, "your creations are as breathtaking as they are intriguing."

Elara, ever enigmatic, smiled. "Just a touch of clockwork magic to spice up the night," she replied, her voice tinkling like chimes. "But tell me, what secrets does your mask hold?"

Their conversation, a veiled dance of words and hidden identities, became the first waltz of the night. Soon, others joined, their masks as diverse as their stories. A jester, his wit as sharp as his blade, traded barbs with a regal-looking figure whose mask shimmered with an otherworldly light.

Meanwhile, Elara's clockwork creations flitted about, each butterfly carrying a unique task. One, adorned with gears like miniature planets, guided lost souls to hidden corners where whispered conversations blossomed. Another, its wings painted with scenes of forgotten stories, sparked impromptu performances, transforming the ballroom into a stage for shared dreams.

As the night deepened, the masks seemed to melt away. A shy scholar, emboldened by a mask that resembled a mythical beast, confessed his love to a scientist, her mask adorned with constellations. A seasoned warrior, his mask a grizzled wolf, shared his war stories with a young apprentice, her mask a blooming flower.

Elara, watching the connections bloom under the watchful gaze of the moon, knew her magic had gone beyond clockwork and gears. It had unlocked the stories hidden within each mask, the vulnerabilities and desires that bound them all together.

As dawn painted the sky with the first blush of light, the guests, their faces now revealed, shared smiles and newfound connections. The House of Whispers, its secrets momentarily unveiled, held the echoes of laughter, shared dreams, and a touch of clockwork magic.

Elara, amidst the departing crowd, dismantled her clockwork butterflies. The magic, she knew, wasn't in the gears or the masks, but in the stories whispered, the connections forged, and the realization that even in a masked world, the most beautiful magic was the one that resided within each heart. The party might have ended, but the stories, like the faint scent of perfume and the lingering melody of laughter, would carry on, a testament to the magic ignited within the House of Whispers.

Here is the story behind 6X8.

I am a hacker and a rapper, who uses my skills to expose the corruption and injustice in the world. We are part of a group called KPG, who are known for their daring and controversial hacks and songs. We believe that we are fighting for a noble cause, and that we are the only ones who can see through the lies and manipulation of the system.

But our actions also attract the attention of the authorities, who are determined to stop us and our group. I am eventually tracked down and arrested, and thrown into a 6x8 cell, where you are isolated and interrogated. I feel like I have lost everything: My freedom, my voice, my friends, my purpose. I resort to taking pills to numb the pain and the fear, but they only make me more paranoid and depressed. I wonder if I will ever get out of this prison, and if God is watching over me and my people.

But I also refuse to give up hope. I decide to use my time in prison to write new lyrics and code, that I hope will reach the outside world and inspire others to join our cause. I want to show that I am not a criminal, but a rebel, and that I have a message and a vision for a better world. You want to prove that I am still alive, and that I still have something to say. I want to become a legend, and a hero.
